articleTitle: Transforming Multidimensional Time Series into Interpretable Event Sequences for Advanced Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel spatiotemporal feature representation model designed to address the limitations of traditional methods in multidimensional time series (MTS) analysis. The proposed approach converts MTS into one-dimensional sequences of spatially evolving events, preserving the complex coupling relationships between dimensions. By employing a variable-length tuple mining method, key spatiotemporal features are extracted, enhancing the interpretability and accuracy of time series analysis. Unlike conventional models, this unsupervised method does not rely on large training datasets, making it adaptable across different domains. Experimental results from motion sequence classification validate the model's superior performance in capturing intricate patterns within the data. The proposed framework has significant potential for applications across various fields, including backend services for monitoring and optimizing IT infrastructure, medical diagnosis through continuous patient monitoring and health trend analysis, and internet businesses for tracking user behavior and forecasting sales. This work offers a new theoretical foundation and technical support for advancing time series data mining and its practical applications in human behavior recognition and other domains.

articleTitle: Optimizing News Text Classification with Bi-LSTM and Attention Mechanism for Efficient Data Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The development of Internet technology has led to a rapid increase in news information. Filtering out valuable content from complex information has become an urgent problem that needs to be solved. In view of the shortcomings of traditional manual classification methods that are time-consuming and inefficient, this paper proposes an automatic classification scheme for news texts based on deep learning. This solution achieves efficient classification and management of news texts by introducing advanced machine learning algorithms, especially an optimization model that combines Bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory Network (Bi-LSTM) and Attention Mechanism. Experimental results show that this solution can not only significantly improve the accuracy and timeliness of classification, but also significantly reduce the need for manual intervention. It has important practical significance for improving the information processing capabilities of the news industry and accelerating the speed of information flow. Through comparative analysis of multiple common models, the effectiveness and advancement of the proposed method are proved, laying a solid foundation for future news text classification research.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning for Knowledge-Based Question Generation in Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, especially the increasingly widespread application of question-and-answer systems, high-quality question generation has become a key component in supporting the development of these systems. This article focuses on knowledge-based question generation technology, which aims to enable computers to simulate the human questioning process based on understanding specific texts or knowledge bases. In light of the issues of hallucination and knowledge gaps present in large-scale language models when applied to knowledge-intensive tasks, this paper proposes an enhanced question generation method that incorporates contrastive learning. This method utilizes multiple models to jointly mine domain knowledge and uses contrastive learning to guide the model in reducing noise and hallucinations in generation. Experimental results show that by designing prompts containing contrasting examples, the model's performance in question generation improves considerably, particularly when contrasting instructions and examples are used simultaneously, leading to the highest quality of generated questions and improved accuracy. These results demonstrate that the method proposed in this study, which combines contrasting context and chain-of-thought prompts, can effectively improve both the quality and the practicality of question generation.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Potential of Graph Neural Networks in SME Credit Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper takes the graph neural network as the technical framework, integrates the intrinsic connections between enterprise financial indicators, and proposes a model for enterprise credit risk assessment. The main research work includes: Firstly, based on the experience of predecessors, we selected 29 enterprise financial data indicators, abstracted each indicator as a vertex, deeply analyzed the relationships between the indicators, constructed a similarity matrix of indicators, and used the maximum spanning tree algorithm to achieve the graph structure mapping of enterprises; secondly, in the representation learning phase of the mapped graph, a graph neural network model was built to obtain its embedded representation. The feature vector of each node was expanded to 32 dimensions, and three GraphSAGE operations were performed on the graph, with the results pooled using the Pool operation, and the final output of three feature vectors was averaged to obtain the graph's embedded representation; finally, a classifier was constructed using a two-layer fully connected network to complete the prediction task. Experimental results on real enterprise data show that the model proposed in this paper can well complete the multi-level credit level estimation of enterprises. Furthermore, the tree-structured graph mapping deeply portrays the intrinsic connections of various indicator data of the company, and according to the ROC and other evaluation criteria, the model's classification effect is significant and has good “robustness”.

articleTitle: Development and Application of a Monte Carlo Tree Search Algorithm for Simulating Da Vinci Code Game Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In this study, we explore the efficiency of the Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS), a prominent decision-making algorithm renowned for its effectiveness in complex decision environments, contingent upon the volume of simulations conducted. Notwithstanding its broad applicability, the algorithm's performance can be adversely impacted in certain scenarios, particularly within the domain of game strategy development. This research posits that the inherent branch divergence within the Da Vinci Code board game significantly impedes parallelism when executed on Graphics Processing Units (GPUs). To investigate this hypothesis, we implemented and meticulously evaluated two variants of the MCTS algorithm, specifically designed to assess the impact of branch divergence on computational performance. Our comparative analysis reveals a linear improvement in performance with the CPU-based implementation, in stark contrast to the GPU implementation, which exhibits a non-linear enhancement pattern and discernible performance troughs. These findings contribute to a deeper understanding of the MCTS algorithm's behavior in divergent branch scenarios, highlighting critical considerations for optimizing game strategy algorithms on parallel computing architectures.

articleTitle: A Lightweight Adaptive Filtering Network for Efficient Image Dehazing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In recent years, seeking image dehazing solutions in the frequency domain has gained significant attention. However, current methods are insufficient in flexibly selecting the most informative frequency components for restoration, and considering all frequency domain components introduces redundant information from irrelevant regions. In this paper, we propose a lightweight adaptive filtering network (AFNet), which primarily includes an Adaptive Filtering Module (AFM) designed to select the most informative frequency components while removing feature redundancy in both the frequency and channel domains. The AFM consists of two parts: an Adaptive Frequency Filtering Module (AFFM) and a Channel Refinement Feedforward Module (CRFM). Specifically, the AFFM employs a dual-branch adaptive computation, where one branch selects the most informative components in the frequency domain and removes redundant information and noise interactions, while the other branch ensures the network receives sufficient information flow to learn discriminative representations. Simultaneously, the designed CRFM incorporates channel attention and gating mechanisms into the feedforward network to eliminate feature redundancy in the channels, thereby enhancing the restoration of clear latent images by utilizing important channels. Experimental results on commonly used benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed AFFM and CRFM. For example, AFNet achieves a PSNR of 41.68 dB on the SOTS indoor dataset with only 2.42 million parameters.

articleTitle: Realtime Scene Enhancement of Low Light Image/Video
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The quality of image and videos plays a vital role in case of real-time systems. Images are captured without sufficient illumination, lead to low dynamic range and high propensity for generating high noise levels. The processing ideas and networks of several mainstream low-light image enhancement neural network algorithms such as DRBN, DSLR, ZeroDCE, EnlightenGAN, as well as the key technologies used are compared and analyzed. In this paper, the EnglightenGAN neural network is used as the core image enhancement algorithm, and NVIDIA AGX Xavier equipment and video stream processing technology are used to achieve the entire process of video acquisition, video frame encoding, image enhancement processing, frame decoding, and video stream display. It can adapt to most low-light and dark scenes which has a good enhancement effect on video streams collected in low-light scenes. The real-time performance and image enhancement effect of the system achieved good results, with FPS reaching 10, SSIM reaching 0.51753, and PSNR reaching 27.89973.

articleTitle: Efficient Mastery of Gomoku Game Through Deep Monte Carlo Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Deep reinforcement learning has made significant progress in the field of computer games. Traditional methods typically involve extensive tree expansion and simulation during the self-play phase to generate large amounts of match data for training models, which requires substantial computational resources. To reduce reliance on high computational resources, we abandoned the traditional self-play method and adopted a deep Monte Carlo method to generate match data in batches on GPUs, without relying on tree expansion. When applying this method to the game of Gomoku, the results showed that under limited computational resources, this method achieved a faster increase in Elo rating compared to traditional methods and exhibited faster convergence during training. Moreover, agents using this method ranked first among 503 agents on Peking University's BotZone platform.

articleTitle: Cross-Subject Driver Fatigue Detection Based on Attention-Guided Multi-Scale Convolutional Neural Networks Using EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Fatigue driving is one of the main causes of traffic accidents worldwide. Research shows that around 20% of traffic accidents are closely related to driver fatigue. Therefore, establishing a reliable and accurate driver fatigue detection model is crucial to reducing traffic accidents and improving road safety. Physiological signals such as electroencephalograms (EEG) can more directly reflect the driver's physiological state, thus offering higher detection accuracy. However, most existing CNN-based methods focus only on single-scale EEG feature extraction, failing to capture fine-grained characteristics comprehensively. Moreover, many researchers concentrate only on single-channel EEG fatigue detection, which can lead to information loss or redundancy. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multi-scale convolutional neural network (MSCNN) guided by a channel attention mechanism (CAM). The MSCNN captures multi-dimensional features of EEG signals, while the CAM explores channel contributions, emphasizing more valuable information to complement the MSCNN's performance. Our method achieves satisfactory results on the SADT public dataset, with an average accuracy of 79.62% across 11 subjects, outperforming other fatigue detection methods. This demonstrates that our model is effective in EEG-based driver fatigue detection.

articleTitle: A New Paradigm for Deep Micro-Expression Recognition Under Occluded Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Micro-expression recognition is a pivotal task in facial analysis, focusing on detecting and analyzing subtle, fleeting changes in facial expressions. However, in real-world applications, facial regions are often obscured by objects like glasses, leading to feature loss and a marked decline in recognition accuracy. To overcome this challenge, we introduces a dual-branch neural network model that leverages feature restoration(DBFRNet) for recognizing occluded micro-expression. The first branch leverages the Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model to progressively reconstruct occluded facial regions using conditional generation and multi-step sampling, ensuring harmony between the restored and visible regions. The second branch extracts temporal dynamic features of the face using optical flow techniques, while a visual Transformer encoder enhances the spatial feature representation. Through a coordinate attention mechanism, the outputs of both branches are effectively integrated in the feature fusion layer, enhancing the overall performance of micro-expression recognition in scenarios with significant occlusions. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance on multiple simulated occlusion micro-expression datasets, significantly improving both accuracy and robustness.

articleTitle: Quantitative Research on Complexity of Urban Environment Based on AI Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Visual complexity is a pivotal metric in urban environment quality, and the objective quantification of visual complexity holds immense importance for research in this field. Drawing from the definition of visual complexity, this paper categorizes complexity into environmental element feature complexity, Edge Feature Complexity, and color complexity. By harnessing computer image processing technology and incorporating artificial intelligence methodologies, the study successfully deploys a supervised training model to amalgamate these multiple features, which created a preliminary framework for quantifying visual complexity, offering valuable insights for future investigations into human aesthetic experiences and urban visual quality assessments.

articleTitle: The Data-Reusing Maximum Correlation Entropy Algorithm Based with Logarithmic Functions
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The data-reusing maximum correlation entropy algorithm (DRMCC) exhibits good convergence characteristics in adaptive filters when the input data are correlated. To further enhance the estimation performance of this algorithm for sparse systems, a penalty term in the form of a logarithmic function is incorporated, leading to the proposal of a logarithmic functionbased data-reusing maximum correlation entropy algorithm (DRMCCLZA). The penalty term imposes varying degrees of zero-attraction for distinct weight coefficients, enabling the algorithm to adjust the magnitude of zero-attraction in real time, contingent on the fluctuations of the weight coefficients throughout the update iteration process. The theoretical analysis of the convergence of the DRMCCLZA algorithm is presented herewith. The results of the simulation experiments demonstrate that the algorithm exhibits superior performance compared to other similar algorithms in system identification scenarios. Additionally, the algorithm demonstrates enhanced robustness in the context of sparse systems.

articleTitle: Meta-Heuristic Hyperparametric Optimization Model BO-GCN-LSTM for Spatial Interaction-Oriented Prediction Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Understanding spatial interactions is crucial for analyzing human activities across regions, yet predicting these interactions between cities on a large scale remains challenging due to the complexity of influencing factors. This study integrates a meta-heuristic optimization algorithm with a deep learning model to enhance the accuracy of such predictions nationwide. A Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) is employed to aggregate geographic features and capture spatial dependencies, while a Long Short-Term Memory Network (LSTM) identifies temporal patterns. To optimize the models, a Bayesian optimization algorithm (BO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) were utilized to search for optimal hyperparameters, resulting in the BO-GCN-LSTM and GA-GCN-LSTM models. Comparative analysis reveals that the MSE values of the BO-GCN-LSTM and GA-GCN-LSTM models are 23% and 22.4% lower, the RMSE values are 23.9% and 15.7% lower, and the R2 values are 18% and 20% higher, respectively, than those of the GCN-LSTM model. These results demonstrate that the BO-GCN-LSTM model is particularly well-suited for large-scale predictions of spatial interactions between cities.

articleTitle: Recognition of Meteorological Conditions in Snowy Days for Transmission Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The stable operation of transmission lines under severe weather conditions is critical to the reliability of power systems. Accurately identifying the state of transmission lines during snowy and other extreme weather conditions can enhance the efficiency of grid maintenance and dispatch. This thesis proposes a computer vision-based method for recognizing the snow weather state of transmission lines. By constructing a dataset of images taken during clear and snowy days, this study compares and analyzes the performance of several deep learning models, including ResNet, RepLKNet, and TinyViT, in snow weather recognition. Experimental results demonstrate that the RepLKNet model exhibits the best accuracy and robustness, effectively distinguishing between clear and snowy weather images with an accuracy of over 99%. Compared to traditional methods, the proposed deep learning-based approach significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of snow weather state recognition for transmission lines. The findings provide technical support for intelligent maintenance of power systems under extreme weather conditions.

articleTitle: Modeling Method of Flight Operation Information Flow Based on TIMED PETRI NET
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Time performance is an important indicator of flight operation program design and evaluation, which affects the time urgency and workload of pilots to perform tasks. The modeling method of flight operation information flow based on the timed Petri net is proposed, and the upper and lower bounds of time constraints for different flight operation types such as serial operation, parallel operation and selection operation are defined. A static time performance analysis method based on network structure characteristics is proposed, and a dynamic time performance analysis method affected by pilot behavior is proposed. Combined with the rejected take-off operation procedure of a certain aircraft, an example of information flow modeling and time performance analysis based on the timed Petri net is given, which demonstrates the feasibility and effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A Steelmaking-continuous Casting Scheduling Optimization Method Considering Time-of-use Electricity Pricing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Small-scale scrap metal recycling and remanufacturing enterprises show great potential in the situation of green transformation and sustainable development faced by the steel industry. It has the main advantages of protecting the environment and saving resources. However the production planning and energy consumption problems of steelmaking-continuous casting (SCC) plague its development. In light of these considerations, this paper proposes an enhanced gray wolf optimization algorithm, designated as Q-GWO, which incorporates Q-Iearning to address the scheduling challenges associated with SCC under the influence of time-of-use electricity pricing. The method was tested in the context of production scheduling for a small scrap metal recycling and remanufacturing enterprise in Guangdong. The results demonstrated that the algorithm is capable of effectively scheduling the production process, optimizing the makespan, and initiating high-energy-consuming processes during periods of low electricity prices, thereby minimizing the total electricity cost. Furthermore, comparative experiments were conducted with the common Dynamic Programming (DP) algorithm, Gray Wolf Optimization (GWO) algorithm, and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The results demonstrated that the proposed algorithm exhibited superior performance compared to the other comparative algorithms.

articleTitle: IRS-Assisted Secrecy Rate Maximization for Visible Light Communication Based on Improved Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Intelligent reflective surfaces (IRS), as an emerging channel tuning technique, have been widely used in visible light communication(VLC) systems. We look at how to adjust the correspondence between the IRS and the transceiver so that the communication system maximizes the secrecy rate while satisfying the basic communication rate as well as the energy harvesting requirements. To address this assignment problem, a gain particle swarm optimization (GPSO) algorithm that leverages channel gain was proposed, which improves the particle velocity and position updating formula by introducing amplified gain. The experimental results indicate that improved GPSO algorithm compared to the PSO algorithm improves the rate by 8Mbit/s under the constraints and the energy harvesting by 5mJ, at the same time, we can see that the GPSO algorithm also has a performance advantage over the SCA and DE algorithms, these results show that GPSO algorithm can be well applied to this kind of allocation problem.

articleTitle: PMSNeRF: Patch-Based Neural Radiance Fields for Generalizable Multi-View Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) has achieved notable advancements in neural reconstruction and rendering, but it faces challenges with long rendering times for each scene and struggles to generalize new scenes. We introduce a new multi-view reconstruction technique called PMSNeRF. This method significantly improves the ability to generalize and the quality of novel view synthesis. By incorporating the shallow layers of the Visual Geometry Group (VGG) network to extract patch features from target views and enhancing local features during training, our model is better equipped to capture differences in images, leading to improved reconstruction outcomes. Drawing inspiration from a Two Time-Scale Update Rule (TTUR), we perform patch extraction every 64 steps, which boosts training efficiency and optimizes overall model performance while making effective use of computational resources. Our results show that PMSNeRF surpasses various generalizable NeRF models across multiple synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating clear advantages in managing rendering artifacts and complex geometric structures. The methodology we propose holds significant potential for applications in various domains, including robotics, virtual reality, and augmented reality.

articleTitle: UAV-Assisted Fog Computing Offloading Strategy Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the arrival of the Internet of Things era, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication become more popular due to their high maneuverability and low operating costs. In this paper, a UAV equipped a fog computing server used to provide computing offloading services for user equipments (UEs). Under the constraint of certain energy consumption, we jointly optimize user scheduling, computing resource allocation, UAV flight direction and speed to achieve the optimization goal of minimizing the maximum processing delay. The deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) offloading algorithm improved by a priority experience replay (PER) pool can increase the probability of high-value sampling and solve the problem of sparse rewards. We introduce the DDPG-PER offloading algorithm into this scene to achieve minimize the maximum processing delay and design experiments to compare with other algorithms. Experiments show that the DDPG-PER offloading algorithm can quickly achieve the optimization goals of convergence. The proposed DDPG-PER algorithm can faster achieve convergence always has lower delay compared with other benchmark algorithms in different task size. Meanwhile, in different computing capability of UAV, it has a better performance on offloading ratio and decreasing delay compared with the other benchmark algorithm.

articleTitle: A DCDP-Net Speech Enhancement Model for Parallel Denoising of Amplitude and Phase Spectra
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose DCDP-Net for real-time speech enhancement in the time-frequency domain, which denoises both the magnitude and phase spectra. DCDP-Net uses an encoder-decoder architecture connected by a dilated complex dual-path conformer (DCDP-Conformer). The DCDP-Conformer adds temporal and frequency attention to capture speech information in both domains. The encoder processes the noisy input, while the decoder, consisting of a magnitude mask decoder and a phase decoder, recovers the clean speech. Experiments show that DCDP-Net achieves a PESQ of 3.05 on the VoiceBank+DEMAND dataset, outperforming baseline models. Ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each module.

articleTitle: SD-MTMA: Integrating Static and Dynamic Methods for Detecting Multi-Trigger Multi-Action Rule Conflicts in Smart Homes
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Smart homes are a key application of the Internet of Things, where users employ Trigger-Action Programming rules for personalized control. However, as the number of rules increases, conflicts arise, disrupting system operations. This study proposes a novel method to automatically detect these conflicts by combining static and dynamic approaches. The static method detects and resolves rule conflicts, while dynamic detection is performed across multiple scenarios generated from user-defined rules, enhancing accuracy. For conflicts involving device impacts, this study proposes the “opposing function extraction method,” and uses cosine similarity to calculate environmental impacts, minimizing manual intervention. A dataset of 20,537 complex rules was constructed for validation. Experimental results show that the method achieves a precision of 0.95, recall of 0.81, and F1-score of 0.88. Compared with UTEA, CDAM, and KGIBE, this approach significantly reduces manual annotation needs and improves conflict detection, CPU usage, and memory efficiency.

articleTitle: Semantic Segmentation Algorithm of Nighttime Road Surface Water Based on Improved Low-Light Image Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: At present, when semantic segmentation algorithms with high segmentation performance in daytime scenes are directly applied to nighttime scenes, it is difficult to annotate data due to the influence of light and low visibility, especially in the segmentation task of road surface water logging in urban waterlogging monitoring, the effect of water reflection is enhanced, resulting in poor segmentation results. Therefore, this paper proposes a semantic segmentation algorithm for nighttime road flooding. The algorithm introduces SCI low-light image enhancement network to enhance the nighttime road surface water images to reduce the influence of light, and adds a feature enhancement module to solve the problem of image detail loss. At the same time, the spatial attention mechanism is introduced to solve the problem of excessive enhancement and distortion in local areas with good light. Finally, the fusion effect is verified by the Upernet-Swein-T semantic segmentation model. The results show that the mIoU of the fused algorithm reaches 90.03%, which is 1.7% higher than that of the original model algorithm, and the ability of predicting night road surface water is improved.

articleTitle: Mobile Robot Navigation in an Unknown Environment Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper studies an end-to-end navigation method based on deep reinforcement learning, which enables mobile robots to independently explore and navigate in unknown environments using only sensor data and without map information. In this paper, we propose an improved deep reinforcement learning method, design a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) optimization model, optimize the experience pool to improve the utilization rate of valuable positive reward transfer samples, and introduce a goal orientation strategy to help the robot avoid blind exploration. Experimental results show that the proposed optimization model could realize path planning and dynamic obstacle avoidance for mobile robots in complex environments. The convergence speed, planning success rate, and path precision were improved to a certain extent. Compared with the traditional DRL method, the robot's exploration efficiency was higher, and the learned strategies were more reliable.

articleTitle: Intelligent Test Paper Generation Algorithm Integrating Normal Distribution and Parallel Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Genetic algorithms have been widely used in intelligent test paper generation systems. However, traditional genetic algorithms cannot ensure that the difficulty of test questions is normally distributed, and are prone to falling into local optimal solutions. To address the above problems, we proposed an intelligent test paper generation algorithm that combines normal distribution and parallel genetic algorithms. In the population initialization stage, we use the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the normal distribution to initialize the population. In the subsequent genetic operations, we designed a directed mutation mechanism and added KL divergence as a penalty number in the design of the fitness function to ensure that the difficulty of the test questions is normally distributed. At the same time, in order to speed up the efficiency of the algorithm and escape from the local optimal solution, an adaptive migration strategy was introduced. Experimental results show that the difficulty of the test questions generated by this algorithm is normally distributed, and the algorithm performance is better than other algorithms.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of EEG-fNIRS Based Brain-Computer Interface Paradigm for Musical Imagery
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In this experiment, EEG-fNIRS simultaneous acquisition technology was used to design and implement a brain-computer interface paradigm for musical imagery, and the self-designed experimental paradigm was utilized for sampling with a size of 40 college student subjects, data processing, time-frequency domain feature extraction, statistical analysis based on EEG, fNIRS in the resting, white noise, listening, and recall phases, and neurovascular coupling were carried out. Finally, music recognition based on six songs was performed by machine learning, resulting in the best recognized song as well as its features. In the future, the construction of a multimodal database based on simple elements of musical imagery is planned.

articleTitle: Mathematical Modeling of the Expanding Square Search Pattern of the Lost Submersible
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In this article, the Expanding Square Search Pattern is introduced for locating missing submersibles in three-dimensional ocean environments. Initial deployment points are set based on the highest probability density from the positioning model, and the optimal search area is established using anticipated probabilities. Following discretization, an Expanding Square Search Pattern is adopted within the horizontal plane plus vertical scanning to search the space. Indefinite integration is performed over the scanned space using the probability density matrix, ultimately deriving a function that links search probability to time.

articleTitle: Fuzzy Overlapping Community Guided Hierarchical Self-Attention Pooling
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Graph pooling aims at extracting vital information for graph coarsening, and thus helping graph neural networks to improve their graph representation ability. However, existing methods either compress similar nodes by a clustering algorithm or discard unimportant nodes by an importance score, resulting in the coarsened graph suffering from different issues. Therefore, aiming at the goal of breaking through their limitation, this paper develops a fuzzy overlapping community guided hierarchical self-attention pooling, namely FOCoHSAP. FOCoHSAP performs node selection within every detected community rather than the entire graph, which allows for an explicit preservation of both topology hierarchy and detailed node information. Especially, FOCoHSAP introduces fuzzy overlapping community detection algorithm to explore those fine-grained relationships between nodes and communities, allowing for a more promising learning of graph representation that can be utilized for accurate graph classification.

articleTitle: An Improved Method for Control Dependency in LLVM
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The existence of control dependencies within programs necessitates intricate data reorganization, significantly hindering the vectorization capabilities in automated SIMD compilation processes. The latest iteration of the LLVM compiler, employs a control flow vectorization approach that is contingent upon platform-specific mask intrinsic functions. This reliance results in many loops with IF constructs forfeiting their vectorization potential. To address this, a novel mask instruction transformation technique is introduced, converting IF structures to select instructions. This conversion facilitates control flow vectorization independent of intrinsic functions, effectively transitioning from control to data dependencies. Furthermore, an enhancement to the existing Phi node generation algorithm is proposed to augment control flow vectorization opportunities. Utilizing the TSVC benchmark suite, the experimental results demonstrate a 48% increase in vectorization recognition rate following the implementation of the mask instruction transformation. The maximum speedup ratio achieved is 2.4, with an average speedup ratio of 1.6, outperforming LLVM's current automatic vectorization capabilities.

articleTitle: Detection of Driver's Emergency Braking Intention in Single-Pedal Control Systems Basing EEG Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In automotive safety and intelligent transport systems, detecting a driver's emergency brake intention is crucial for improving driving safety. Traditional methods rely heavily on driver actions, resulting in slow response times, low accuracy, and difficulty adapting to individual differences and complex driving environments. Recently, physiological signal detection and driver behavior analysis have gained attention for their ability to provide faster, more accurate responses and better adaptability. This study proposes an electroencephalogram (EEG) signal-based method for detecting emergency braking intentions. EEG signals were collected from 12 participants in a simulated driving environment. Features were extracted using Adaptive Power Spectral Density (APSD) and classified using Regular Linear Discriminant Analysis (RLDA) for real-time detection of drivers' emergency braking intentions. This approach enhances vehicle safety and response speed in critical situations and provides technical support and a theoretical basis for the practical application of emergency braking intention detection in single-pedal control systems.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning-Based User Intent Recognition in Human-Computer Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the rapid development of human-computer interaction (HCI) technology, accurately recognizing user intent has become crucial for enhancing user experience. This paper focuses on deep learning-based user intent recognition technology and explores its innovative applications in HCI. We first review recent advances in deep learning in the field of natural language processing, particularly its superior performance in user intent recognition tasks. By constructing deep learning models such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTMs), and Transformers, this research aims to extract high-level features from user input data including text, speech, or behavioral data to achieve precise user intent recognition.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition Based on Neural Networks and Accelerators
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This study aims to recognise accelerometer-based human activities using ANN models. We used the UCI-HAR dataset, which is a widely used publicly available dataset containing accelerometer data for six daily activities (walking, walking up stairs, walking down stairs, sitting, standing and lying down). In order to improve the accuracy of the recognition, we performed detailed pre-processing of the data, including data cleaning, feature extraction and normalisation. The preprocessed data is fed into the designed ANN model. During the model training process, we used the prediction rate, recall rate and F1 score as performance evaluation metrics. The experimental results show that our ANN model can effectively recognise different activity types, showing high accuracy and robustness. This study not only provides a new approach for human activity recognition, but also provides a valuable reference for the development of intelligent health monitoring systems.

articleTitle: Task Separation and Knowledge Sharing for Class Incremental Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Methods based on dynamically expanding architectures can effectively mitigate catastrophic forgetting in class incremental learning (CIL), but they often overlook information sharing and integration between subnetworks, leading to performance degradation and increased parameter count and memory consumption as the network expands. To address these complex issues, we introduce a new method called Task Separation and Knowledge Sharing (TSKS), which transfers knowledge at both the logical and feature levels through Hybrid Knowledge Distillation (HKD). In logical distillation, we combine Global Knowledge Distillation (GKD) and Task Knowledge Distillation (TKD) to establish connections between tasks. To prevent the model from favoring new classes, we design an Attention- Based Feature Fusion (ABFF) mechanism to capture important features. Additionally, we introduce a Soft-Margin Auxiliary Loss (SMAL) to help the model learn new concepts. Extensive experiments show that TSKS outperforms existing models on CIFAR100 and ImageNet100, regardless of whether memory samples are used. Notably, TSKS demonstrates superior performance in memory-free settings, indicating a reduced reliance on rehearsal memory.

articleTitle: Research on Fluorescent Magnetic Particle Inspection of Industrial Part Defects Based on Improved YOLOv5
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: To meet rising quality inspection demands in industrial automation, this study presents an enhanced YOLOv5 model for detecting minor surface defects in industrial parts through fluorescent magnetic particle inspection (FMPI). Traditional FMPI relies on inefficient and subjective manual checks. Our improved model, featuring a Channel-Attention module and optimized for a custom dataset, significantly boosts detection precision and speed. Experiments confirm its superior performance over conventional methods, offering a robust solution for automated non-destructive testing.

articleTitle: Analysis of Suicide Factors in the Chinese Population Based on Non-Negative Matrix Factorization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper analyzes the factors that contribute to suicide and proposes an innovative suicide tendency prediction model based on the NMF algorithm. Using 52 suicide samples from newspaper reports, assisted by the SVD algorithm, it is found that sui-cide can be better explained by implicit factors instead of explicit ones, and the NMF algorithm is more effective than MLR in sui-cide prediction. The magnitude of the Frobenius Norm of NMF is the quantitative expression to evaluate one's suicide tendency, where a higher Frobenius Norm indicates a lower suicide propensity. The theoretical and practical implications are discussed.

articleTitle: D-CBAMFi: A Lightweight Multi-Scale Fusion Network Based on Depthwise Separable Convolution and Dilated Convolution
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Gesture recognition is crucial for the development of new human-computer interaction paradigms that will change the interaction between humans and their surroundings. Most deep learning-based techniques use neural networks with a single backbone architecture, which can only capture a single feature and cannot meet the requirements of real-world applications for recognition tasks in resource-limited and complex scenarios. Therefore, we propose a lightweight multi-scale fusion network, D-CBAMFi, whose core component is a D-CBAM network consisting of parallel depth-wise separable convolution and dilated convolution and CBAM. The proposed system achieves an average accuracy of 84.30% on the Widar dataset, validating the effectiveness of the model.

articleTitle: TL-DREN: Transfer Learning Based Detection and Recognition of Electricity Nameplates
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach that integrates traditional image processing techniques with deep learning to enhance the accuracy and robustness of fuzzy text detection and recognition in nameplate images of power equipment. Initially, traditional methods are employed to locate the nameplate and extract information, followed by perspective transformation to correct image distortions. Subsequently, deep learning models are utilized for text detection and recognition. Two specialized datasets were constructed for this study: one for text detection, comprising 841 high-resolution images captured under various environmental conditions, and another for text recognition, consisting of 42,556 cropped text region images derived from the corrected nameplate images. The PP-OCRv4 model was fine-tuned on our curated dataset to improve its performance on text detection and recognition tasks specific to power equipment nameplates. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method achieved an F1-score of 0.524 for text detection and an accuracy of 0.82 for text recognition, showcasing the potential of this approach to enhance the efficiency of automated management of power equipment.

articleTitle: Research on the Stowage Planning Model and Algorithms for Container Ships Considering Out-of-Gauge (OOG) Containers
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative optimization framework grounded in integer linear programming, meticulously examining pivotal factors encompassing container dimensions, varieties, weights, and destination ports. The model surpasses conventional approaches by meticulously orchestrating not just standard container stowage but also ensuring the judicious placement of specialized containers, notably out-of-gauge (OOG) units, thereby enhancing cargo security and transportation efficacy. By meticulously integrating multifaceted constraints-encompassing slot capacity thresholds, balanced weight distribution imperatives, and compatibility considerations among diverse container types—this model adeptly tackles intricate vessel stowage challenges. Experimental validations underscore its prowess in substantially elevating container loading ratios while concurrently safeguarding vessel stability. Consequently, it offers shipping enterprises a scientific and pragmatic decision-making tool, fostering operational excellence and competitive advantage.

articleTitle: Posture Planning Study of Manual Assembly Operations in Narrow Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Aiming at the constraints of manual assembly operation in narrow space, a multi-objective attitude optimization model is constructed by combining the balance, reachability, collision detection and other factors of human attitude. Specifically, the coupling relationship between the manual assembly operation posture in narrow space and the balance, target visibility, joint angle and operation target reachability is first analyzed. Then, the functional relationship between the human assembly operation posture and the above influencing factors is established, and the multi-objective optimization model of the assembly operation posture in narrow space is constructed. Finally, NSGA-III(Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III) multi-objective genetic algorithm is used to solve the model and realize the attitude planning of assembly operation in narrow space.

articleTitle: Rolling Bearing Fault Diagnosis Based on SCSO-LightGBM
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Given the frequent occurrence of rolling bearing faults, to effectively enhance the accuracy of rolling bearing fault diagnosis, this paper constructs a bearing fault diagnosis classifier using a Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), and applies Sand Cat Swarm Optimization (SCSO) to optimize the optimal hyperparameters, constructing a SCSO- LightGBM model. To avoid the lack of feature extraction at a single scale, the temporal domain and spectral domain features of rolling bearing vibration signals are extracted as fault features. The results show that the SCSO-LightGBM model presented in this paper can diagnose the rolling bearing fault type more accurately, and its classification performance exceeds that of other comparison models.

articleTitle: Intelligent Error Correction Method for Electric Power Text Based on ELECTRA
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In the power industry, text information processing is a crucial task. Whether it's a day-to-day official document release, news writing, or an editorial response to a text related to the power system, a large amount of textual information needs to be processed precisely. With the continuous progress of technology and the expansion of application scope, text correction technology will bring more innovation and development opportunities to the power industry, and is of great significance to facilitate the sustainable progress of the power industry. In this paper, the statistical language model and the neural network-based pre-trained model are fused to train and verify the correction of typos in the power text, and finally the model effect is evaluated through the comprehensive index F1. The results show that the F1 values of the single pre-trained model and the single statistical language model are 0.5871 to 0.4738, respectively, which is lower than the F1 of the fusion model for text typo correction of 0.6354. This fusion method has a good effect on text typo correction in the power industry, and makes a positive impact in ensuring the quality of text related to the power system.

articleTitle: Evaluating Actuarial Present Values in Continuous Annuities Under the Hossian Assumption: A Case Study of Main Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The lifespan of grid equipment plays a pivotal role in determining equipment renewal strategies. In calculating the actuarial present value, adopting a segmented lifespan hypothesis becomes essential for accuracy. It is evident that the validity of this Hypothesis significantly enhances the precision in forecasting grid equipment lifespan. When compared with other conventional assumption, the segmented lifespan approach enables a more thorough integration of failure data drawn from life tables. Moreover, this Hypothesis facilitates a continuous failure rate estimation across the entire lifecycle of grid equipment, while also offering additional beneficial geometric properties. In this study, the Hossion Hypothesis is utilized to assess the reliability of segmented lifespan failure rate estimations. Drawing on the Hossion Hypothesis, this work delves into the actuarial present value computations for two distinct categories of continuous service lives. Furthermore, this study employs life tables from key equipment of the China Southern Power Grid (2020–2023, main transformer) to conduct numerical analyses, followed by a comparison with the Balducci Hypothesis results. Through this comparative analysis, the study illustrates the advantages of the Hossion Hypothesis in actuarial present value estimation, and substantiates its potential to improve the precision of failure rate predictions.

articleTitle: Research on Personalized Product Recommendation Algorithm Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In view of the insufficiency of feature information utilization and overfitting in the recommendation task of Transformer network, this paper proposes a model combining random shared embeddings and multi-layer multi-head attention blocks to solve the problems still existing in the above deep learning-based recommendation algorithm. Aiming at the problem of multi-feature information utilization, this paper studies the use of multi-layer multi-head attention block to fuse multi-information. CARCA-SSE model is designed in this paper. Different from traditional location embedding, this paper uses the absolute date of user interaction as time embedding to make full use of existing information. To solve the overfitting problem, random shared Embedding is added to the recommended model based on CARCA, and the Embedding layer is randomly replaced by another Embedding with a certain probability. Using the replaced embedding can reduce the risk of overfitting and further improve the generalization ability, thus increasing the robustness of the model.

articleTitle: Auction-Based Information Freshness in 5G Power Communications Relay Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the development of novel power systems, emerging scenarios such as real-time power trading, and real-time control of virtual power plants demand higher standards for the timeliness of power information. We consider a two-way relay network that consists of two users and one relay. Two users are the information sources and destinations of each other, which is cooperative communication. Two users can not connect directly, users finish the transmission through the relay. We propose the auction-based information freshness in two-way relay network. The relay is the auctioneer and users are bidders. We build up Cooperative Game to solve information freshness and prove that there is a unique Nash Equilibrium in relay network. Simulation results validate our theoretical analysis and the impact of information freshness in the system.

articleTitle: Application of XGBoost Model for Predicting Isobaric Heat Capacity of Liquid HC, HFC, and HFO Refrigerants
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This article presents a machine learning model for accurately calculating the isobaric heat capacity of pure HC, HFC, and HFO refrigerants in the liquid phase. Initially, a comprehensive evaluation was conducted on 1687 experimental data points encompassing various refrigerants. Subsequently, distinct linear algorithms, nonlinear algorithms, and ensemble algorithms were individually trained and tested. After careful comparison and analysis, XGBoost emerged as the most effective algorithm for this task. The utilization of XGBoost in predicting and computing the isobaric heat capacity of refrigerants demonstrated excellent agreement with experimental values. The resulting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}^{2}$</tex> value was found to be 0.9734 while RMSE stood at 0.1267 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kJ}/(\text{kg}\cdot \mathrm{K})$</tex>.

articleTitle: Untethered Soft Thin-Film Motor for Portable Human-Machine Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Flexible and lightweight actuators have demonstrated various potential applications in wearable devices, health monitoring systems, and haptic feedback devices. Compared with rigid motors, flexible motors can directly interface with soft human tissue. This paper introduces a soft lightweight thin-film motor driven by electrostatic forces, which can achieve effective vibration control through optimized structural design and material selection. With an overall thickness of approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$350\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, the thin-film motor can produce a vibration displacement of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> under an applied square wave voltage of 280 V at 100 Hz. A mathematical model is proposed to predict the displacement of the thin-film motor at different applied voltages. A miniaturized wireless control circuit has been designed, and integrated with the thin-film motor. The entire untethered flexible motor system significantly enhances its portability. This research demonstrates the effectiveness of the thin-film motor and highlights its potential in wearable devices and interactive systems.

articleTitle: Autoencoder-Based Anomaly Detection Model for Slab Thickness in Continuous Casting
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Real-time anomaly detection of slab thickness is essential for ensuring quality in continuous casting. Existing methods face challenges in data preprocessing and real-time monitoring. This study addresses these issues by integrating Principal Component Analysis for dimensionality reduction and anomaly Detection with an autoencoder model. The proposed approach enables efficient and accurate real-time anomaly detection in slab thickness during the continuous casting process.

articleTitle: Recommendation Algorithms Fusing Knowledge Graph and User Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This Traditional recommendation algorithms fall short in utilizing semantic information, and popular approaches today use graph neural networks (GNNs) to mine the higher-order structure and semantic information of the knowledge graph for recommendation. However, these methods tend to ignore the representation information between items that users have interacted with in their historical interaction behavior. To address this problem, this paper proposes a recommendation model that fuses knowledge graph and user behavior (KGUB). First, the idea of contrastive learning is utilized to encode the interaction patterns of users and items to learn the embedded representations of users. Next, these user embedding vectors are used to feed back the generation of item embedding vectors, by combining the interactions of relationship vectors in the knowledge graph, thus achieving weighted aggregation of the features of the item's neighboring nodes. Finally, the obtained user and item embedding vectors are fused by cross-compression units to capture the higher-order interactions between users and items and perform click-through rate prediction. In order to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the model, comparison experiments are conducted with five baseline models on two public datasets, and the AUC and F1 metrics outperform the other baseline models, demonstrating that the model can provide more accurate recommendation results.

articleTitle: HiLo Optical Sectioning Algorithm Based on the Rolling Ball Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Traditional structured illumination microscopy techniques still face issues such as complex hardware structures, high optical path costs, low efficiency of optical sectioning reconstruction algorithms, and long image acquisition times. To address these problems, this text designs and builds a high-speed portable three-dimensional optical sectioning microscopy system based on DMD and LED, which greatly simplifies the optical path structure and reduces hardware costs. Additionally, through in-depth analysis of traditional optical sectioning reconstruction algorithms, a HiLo optical sectioning reconstruction algorithm based on the rolling ball method (RB-HiLo) is proposed. Experimental results show that compared to the traditional RMS algorithm, this new algorithm improves image acquisition efficiency by 22.8%, enhances optical sectioning reconstruction efficiency by 20.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and demonstrates lower background intensity, more effective deblurring, and higher signal-to-noise ratio in the reconstructed optical sectioning images as indicated by the normalized intensity distribution curves.

articleTitle: DDPG Algorithm with Elastic Replay Buffer Assisting in the Optimization of the NOMA System
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Non-orthogonal multiple access networks inspired by cognitive radio technology can enhance energy efficiency and address the issue of spectrum resource scarcity. However, resource allocation strategies are still needed for optimization. This paper applies deep reinforcement learning (DRL) algorithms to optimize transmission strategies. We propose a DDPG algorithm integrated with elastic experience replay, which helps the agent strike a better balance between exploring new strategies and utilizing existing experiences. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves a higher transmission rate compared to the standard DDPG algorithm, random algorithm and greedy algorithm.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Minimization Scheme with Dynamic Computational Windows for UAV-Assisted Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: As unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) demonstrate significant potential for edge computing, their capacity to rapidly deploy computing services at user locations offers considerable advantages. However, their limited operational time poses a significant challenge for current UAV-assisted edge computing solutions. This paper addresses the optimal scheduling of UAV computing resources and introduces a computing resource scheduling scheme based on dynamic computational windows allocation (CRS-DW). Simulation results demonstrate that the CRS-DW algorithm significantly outperforms existing benchmark algorithms in performance.

articleTitle: Research on Server Fault Prediction Based on Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The concept of fault monitoring system, as the name suggests, is for fault monitoring and detection. Server failure monitoring refers to the system to set monitoring thresholds, you can view in real time, grasp the normal work of the server and the state of failure and when needed, you can query at any time, call the monitoring records. Server failure detection, from the concept of Baidu: failure monitoring system refers to the use of a variety of inspection methods, testing methods, to find the system or equipment whether there is a failure problem detection activities to determine the location of the failure. Fault detection and fault location actually have similar characteristics, they both exist in the network system category, the requirements of the fault location point will be found, give accurate analysis and repair, so as to achieve fault isolation or repair, in order to better run the equipment or system. The process of diagnosing faults is the process of detecting fault problems and isolating them. In this paper, we have studied the prediction of faults in servers based on the foundation of Artificial Intelligence algorithms. The research in this paper provides some research basis and research theory guidance for cross-disciplinary research.

articleTitle: Research on Urban Environmental Sound Classification Model Based on Multi-Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the rapid acceleration of urbanization, the impact of urban environmental sounds is garnering increasing attention. This study aims to develop a classification system capable of swiftly identifying various types of urban environmental sounds, thereby facilitating audio classification and noise pollution management. The research employs a Multi-Convolutional Neural Network (MULT-CNN) algorithm, which enhances the accuracy of audio classification by averaging the results of multiple CNN models. The study utilizes the widely recognized Urbansound8K dataset, which encompasses ten distinct types of urban sounds. Through model training and testing, the system's performance was evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-Score, and processing latency. Experimental results demonstrate that the classification model performs well across most categories, particularly in Category 5 (Engine Idling) and Category 2 (Children Playing), where it achieves high classification accuracy and low processing latency. Additionally, audio classification heatmaps and confusion matrix heatmaps were developed to visually represent the model's effectiveness in audio classification. This research provides an effective technical approach for urban sound classification and management.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis of Hugh Entertainment Strategy Platform Based on Big Data Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the booming development of the leisure and entertainment market, personalization and intelligence have become important criteria for users to choose leisure and entertainment activities. This paper proposes a recreation strategy platform based on big data technology, Zhiqi Xing “Chen”, which aims to provide customized recreation experiences through in-depth analysis of user needs and market dynamics. First, this study reviews the development of big data technology and its application in the field of recreation, and analyzes the shortcomings of the existing recreation strategy platform. Then, the design framework of Zhiqi Xing “Chen” platform is constructed, including the system architecture, functional module division, and user interface design and system testing, focusing on user behavior analysis, content recommendation algorithm design, and personalized service by using the technologies of big data analysis, web crawler, and neural network, etc. Finally, the research results of this recreation platform, discusses its theoretical and practical significance, and looks forward to the future research direction.

articleTitle: Classroom Behavior Recognition Based on YOLOX Improved Feature Redundancy Removal
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The primary objective of researching student classroom behavior recognition and tracking is to systematically collect and identify students' behavior data in the classroom, providing reliable technical support for education and teaching evaluation. Currently, deep learning-based object detection and tracking techniques are the predominant methods for recognizing multiple student targets in the classroom. These techniques utilize deep convolutional neural networks to self-learn from datasets, optimizing models, and improving recognition efficiency. Many algorithms have achieved real-time performance. However, accurately recognizing student classroom behavior remains challenging, particularly in complex classroom environments where accurately identifying small or occluded targets is problematic. This paper proposes a feature redundancy removal method based on improved YOLOX for spatial and channel features, specifically optimized for student classroom behavior recognition and effectively addressing this issue. Experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced model significantly improves recognition efficiency.

articleTitle: Integrated Application of Dispatch Telephone and Human-Machine Workstation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This technology is used to solve the problem of independent and difficult linkage between scheduling telephone and human-machine work services. By establishing a multimedia scheduling communication system for human-machine workstations, the scheduling telephone can be extended to the scheduling data communication network, supporting the integration of scheduling telephone services and scheduling business systems on human-machine workstations. On the one hand, establish a dispatch telephone software terminal system for the human-machine workstation, which is compatible with traditional dispatch stations for answering dispatch calls, and adds proxy answering or dialing of dispatch calls on the human-machine workstation; On the other hand, building a scheduling communication platform for human-machine workstations, providing open interfaces for integration and calling of scheduling business systems, realizing a wider range of intelligent scheduling communication applications such as one click phone call relationship personnel in the plant station diagram, automatic association of plant station information for listening, etc., enabling human-machine workstations to better serve scheduling duty personnel<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>.

Author Keywords: Integration of dispatch telephone and human-machine workstation

articleTitle: Erythemato-Squamous Diseases Diagnosis Based on Support Vector Machine Optimized by Black-Winged Kite Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In response to the difficulty in distinguishing different types of erythemato-squamous diseases, this paper uses support vector machine (SVM) to construct a diagnostic classifier for erythemato-squamous diseases, and optimizes SVM classifier hyperparameters by using black-winged kite algorithm (BKA). Finally, the BKA-SVM classifier for diagnosing erythemato-squamous diseases is established. To test the effectiveness of the classifier, a comparative experiment was conducted with two SVM classifiers optimized by tuna swarm algorithm (TSO) and Osprey optimization algorithm (OOA) respectively. The experimental result indicates that the BKA-SVM classifier has higher accuracy rate in the diagnosis of erythemato-squamous diseases.

articleTitle: Reward Adjustment Mechanism for PUBG Background MAS
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a dynamic reward mechanism for game multi-agents in a two-dimensional simulation environment inspired by the popular game PUBG. The research focuses on improving the learning efficiency and strategic behaviour of agents by dynamically adjusting the reward system based on environmental cues and intelligence performance. This paper proposes a two-tier dynamic reward mechanism, which balances individual and team incentives, with the aim of promoting competitive and cooperative behaviors in highly dynamic and competitive game scenarios.

articleTitle: Improved Daytime Traffic Signal Detection Method Based on YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Addressing current issues such as low accuracy in traffic signal detection algorithms, weak detection capability for small targets, and susceptibility to lighting and vehicle speed variations, we propose an improved traffic signal detection method based on YOLOv8. Initially, an EMA attention mechanism module is incorporated into the backbone network to enhance feature extraction capabilities. Subsequently, the entire Neck module is replaced with ASF's Neck module to improve detection performance for small-scale targets. Further enhancements to the Neck include introducing the P2 small target detection layer to prevent overflow of parameters and computation, thus reducing computational costs. Finally, the original detection head is replaced with SEAMHead, which integrates the SEAM attention mechanism module to compensate for various shortcomings in the original detection head during prediction tasks. Validation on a custom dataset shows that compared to the original YOLOv8, our algorithm achieves a 3.5% increase in accuracy, a 10.3% increase in recall, and an average precision mAP of 93.4%, representing a 5.5% improvement. This method effectively achieves rapid and accurate detection of traffic signals and holds broad applicability for research related to traffic signal analysis on roads.

articleTitle: Applying CycleGAN for Style Transfer of Modern Scenes to Changsha Kiln Patterns in Museum Exhibits
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper explores the possibility of applying Cycle Generative Adversarial Network (CycleGAN) in museums, specifically studying the process of converting modern scene photos into Changsha kiln style patterns. Changsha Kiln, as a famous intangible cultural heritage of Hunan Province, is famous for its unique hand-painted underglaze multicolored technology and diverse styles. However, due to the uniqueness of each ceramic pattern, it is difficult to effectively reproduce and display the unique style and historical background of these patterns in museum displays. This paper proposes a style transfer scheme to convert modern scene images into Changsha kiln style through CycleGAN and apply it in a museum environment. This method not only enhances public participation and museum experience, but also expands the application of CycleGAN in museums and promotes the inheritance and development of cultural heritage.

articleTitle: The Design and Research of a War Game Simulation System for Equipment Support
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: To meet the evolving demands of equipment support in future warfare scenarios, the utilization of war games within the realm of equipment support is being expedited to effectively enhance the efficiency of equipment support. On the basis of explaining the concept of the equipment support war game simulation system, this paper makes an in-depth analysis from three aspects: military requirement, application requirement and system function requirement. Furthermore, it proposes an overall structure for this system based on the implementation process of equipment support. The research findings can serve as a theoretical reference for both the development and practical application of future equipment support war game systems.

articleTitle: Research on Speaker Recognition Based on LPCMCC and PSRCC Fusion Features
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Mel frequency cepstral coefficient (MFCC) is an important feature in speech speaker recognition, and many people like to use MFCC and neural network algorithms to form speaker recognition systems. However, the MFCC coefficient loses the phase information of the speech signal during the extraction process. Therefore, this article proposes a speech recognition method that combines LPC Mel frequency cepstral coefficients (LPCMCC) and phase based spectral root cepstral coefficients (PSRCC). After combining the two, the amplitude and phase information of the speech signal can be compatible and used as input data for the neural network. This article introduces an attention mechanism based on ResNeXT to adjust the weights of feature parameters, highlight key areas, and improve recognition performance. Finally, the AISHELL dataset was used for training and validation, and the experimental results showed that the proposed combined features and improved ResNeXT can effectively improve the accuracy of speaker recognition.

articleTitle: Multi-Scale Visible and Infrared Fusion Target Detection Method Based on a Dual-Branch Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In target detection, efficient fusion of visible and infrared images is crucial. Existing CNNs, which rely on local information extraction, struggle to capture global information, affecting fused image quality. Additionally, fusion networks often lose high-frequency information, reducing target detection accuracy. To address these issues, this paper presents a dual-branch architecture combining a lightweight Transformer with a CNN incorporating CBAM attention mechanisms. The branches handle low-frequency global features and high-frequency local information, improving fused image quality and target detection accuracy. Experiments on MSRS and LLVIP datasets show the proposed algorithm outperforms state-of-the-art methods in fusion performance. Quantitative analysis demonstrates significant improvements in metrics like Information Entropy (EN), Spatial Frequency (SF), and Average Gradient (AG), proving its superiority in detail and frequency representation.

articleTitle: EEG-fNIRS-Based Music Emotion Decoding and Individualized Music Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The relationship between music and the brain is a fascinating and profound area. Previous research has shown that music can profoundly influence brain functions, including emotion.
