Most previous studies have used single-modality neuroimaging techniques such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) to explore the mechanisms of music's effects on the brain. This study used EEG-fNIRS synchronization technology to explore how music regulates emotions by analyzing neurovascular coupling. The results showed that EEG-fNIRS neurovascular coupling results can effectively reflect the differences between different emotions: negative emotion labels show stronger coupling effects than positive emotion labels, and are expected to become a new emotion prediction indicator. In addition, we developed an emotion prediction model by combining an integrated learning model and the PAD emotional three-dimensional model. This model takes into account individual differences in emotional responses and promotes the development of personalized music therapy. This method provides valuable insights into personalized emotion regulation through music, paving the way for future applications of personalized music therapy and generative artificial intelligence customized music creation.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graph Completion Method Based on Graph Contrastive attention Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The goal of knowledge graph completion is to use the existing triplet information in the knowledge base to infer and fill those connections that have not been established. However, most methods deal with triples independently, ignoring the unique heterogeneous structure of knowledge graph and the rich contextual information contained between nodes, which limits the comprehensive mining of triple features. To solve this problem, this paper focuses on the end-to-end knowledge graph completion task and proposes a model called Graph Contrastive Attention Network (GCAT). Through the integrated attention mechanism, GCAT can capture the characteristics of entities and their neighboring relations in the local neighborhood in parallel, and integrate and encapsulate the context information of these entities. To further optimize the representation of triplet features, GCAT introduces a subgraph-level contrastive training strategy, which aims to improve the quality of the generated entity embeddings. To verify the effectiveness of the GCAT model, we conduct an extensive experimental evaluation on the link prediction task. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the GCAT model in predicting missing links in knowledge graphs.

articleTitle: Maximizing Sum Rate in Wireless Communication Systems with Dual Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) has emerged as a promising technology to significantly enhance the performance of wireless communication systems. This paper presents a comprehensive study of a double-IRS assisted multi-user communication system, proposing a novel joint optimization method. A joint optimization approach for passive beamforming in dual IRSs and active beamforming at the base station is applied to maximize the system sum rate. The problem is formulated as a non-convex optimization challenge, addressed through a proposed low-complexity iterative algorithm based on alternating optimization with semi-closed-form solutions. Simulation results validate our theoretical analysis and demonstrate the significant performance advantages of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Breast Ultrasound Tumor Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8s-OBB Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Breast cancer is the most common cancer among women, and early detection and treatment can significantly improve survival rates. Due to its non-radiative nature, effectiveness, and low cost, ultrasound imaging has become a primary tool for breast cancer screening. However, breast ultrasound images typically have low resolution, high noise, and blurred boundaries, making it easy to misdiagnose when relying solely on manual diagnosis. To address these issues, this paper proposes an improved YOLOv8s-OBB algorithm named MS-YOLO for breast ultrasound tumor detection. The model introduces oriented bounding boxes (OBB) to more accurately detect the shape and orientation of tumors and employs deformable convolutional networks (DCNv4) to enhance the model's ability to capture irregular tumor boundaries and complex structures. Additionally, the designed Multi-Scale Feature Focus Pyramid Network (MSFPN) improves the ability to fuse multi-scale information. Experimental results show that MS-YOLO outperforms traditional methods on the BUSI breast ultrasound dataset, particularly in detecting complex backgrounds, demonstrating higher detection accuracy and robustness. This study provides an efficient and accurate solution for breast ultrasound tumor detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing Polyphonic Character Disambiguation in Chinese Text Processing with Bidirectional LSTM Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This study addresses the challenge of polyphonic character ambiguity in Chinese text processing through the development of a deep learning model capable of automatically identifying and resolving such ambiguities. The research begins with data collection and preprocessing, involving the acquisition of polyphonic character text data and a Chinese polyphonic character library, transformed into a suitable format for model input. Subsequently, a model architecture based on a bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network was designed to enhance semantic understanding using 300-dimensional word embedding vectors. While achieving 82.98% accuracy on the test set, the model encountered high loss values during training, indicating potential issues like gradient vanishing. Therefore, future efforts will concentrate on refining the model structure and training methodology to enhance numerical stability and generalization capabilities, aiming for improved performance in real-world polyphonic character disambiguation tasks.

articleTitle: Dynamic Student Classification with Forgetting Mechanisms on Memory Networks for Knowledge Tracing
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Knowledge Tracing (KT), a technique for modeling students' knowledge levels and predicting their future question-answering performance based on their historical answer data, is one of the key research areas to strengthen the ability of personalized education. In recent years, memory networks have received more and more attention and application in the field of KT, however, the current KT model based on memory networks ignores the effect of students' learning sequence on the level of forgetting, and fails to model the forgetting behavior of students in the process of learning by using the characteristics of time intervals in the interaction data. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a dynamic student classification with forgetting mechanisms on memory networks model (DSCFMN), which enhance the existing model by dynamically classifying students similar to their learning abilities at specified time intervals, incorporating forgetting factors and introducing a weight decay strategy. Experiments show that our model performs well on online education datasets, and the proposed model achieves better prediction results than existing knowledge tracking methods.

articleTitle: Comparison of Channel Attention Mechanisms and Graph Attention Mechanisms Applied in Multi-Robot Path Planning Based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are applied to multi-robot path planning due to their advantages in learning communication strategies in decentralized multi-intelligence systems, and to prioritize the important information, we introduce the channel attention mechanism and the graph attention mechanism in GNNs. The channel attention mechanism automatically obtains the importance of each feature channel through network learning, assigns different weight coefficients to each channel, and calculates the importance of each channel of the input image so as to enhance the important features and suppress the unimportant features. Unlike the channel attention mechanism, which calculates the importance of each channel to improve the feature representation, the graph attention mechanism is a new type of neural network that operates on graph-structured data and uses a masked self-attention layer to address the shortcomings of graph convolution-based methods.

articleTitle: Evaluation of In-Vehicle Voice System Based on FAHP-QFD Joint Analysis Method
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The primary mission of an intelligent cabin is to enhance the user experience by meeting users' deep emotional needs. And the in-vehicle voice system is an important tool to achieve this goal, so the evaluation of its usage experience has become a focus of automotive product development. But in addition to functional evaluation, voice interaction systems also involve a lot of subjective perception content, which is difficult to be completed solely by objective testing. Therefore, how to establish a product evaluation theory based on subjective evaluation and bridge the distance between the research and use ends becomes an important proposition. This paper takes the in-vehicle voice system as the research object and attempts to build a scientific performance evaluation method using the combined analysis of fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (FAHP) and quality function deployment (QFD). The rationality of the method is proved through the analysis of practical cases.

articleTitle: Intelligent Error Detection in Electric Power Texts Based on ALBERT-GCNN-CRF Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Detecting grammatical errors in electric power texts is a crucial task in natural language processing, aimed at identifying typos, grammatical issues, and sentence structure problems. Due to the flexibility of grammar and the absence of features such as tense and voice, local information is essential. Traditional machine learning methods often struggle with accuracy, and existing deep learning methods fail to fully leverage local information. We propose a novel model, ALBert-GCNN-CRF, which combines the ALBert pre-trained language model with a convolutional neural network (GCNN) for local information extraction and a residual gating mechanism. This model treats grammatical error detection as a sequence labeling task, using a Conditional Random Field (CRF) to learn relationships between labels. Experimental results show that the ALBert-GCNN-CRF model significantly improves the F1 score for electric power texts, with average increases of 16.9%, 11.2%, and 4.4% compared to other models, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing grammatical error detection.

articleTitle: SOH Estimation and RUL Prediction Framework Based on ED-LightGBM and ED-BiGRU-LA
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: State of health (SOH) estimation and remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are of critical importance to ensure the safety of battery systems. This paper presents an innovative framework for SOH estimation and RUL prediction, i.e., light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) is used to estimate SOH of LIBs and bi-directional gated circulation unit with logsparse attention (BiGRU-LA) is applied to predict LIBs RUL. In order to enhance the model exactness, enterprise development optimization (ED) is used to optimize the hyperparameters of above models. Firstly, it is difficult to measure the capacity of LIBs directly during operation. So, in charging phase, features are extracted from two perspectives i.e. measured variables as well as computed variables. The features exhibiting the strongest correlation with capacity degradation are identified as health indicators (HIs) by using spearman correlation coefficient. Secondly, a single battery is selected for training purpose, while the remaining batteries of the same type are employed to accurately estimate SOH through the utilization of ED-LightGBM feature processing capability. Finally, RUL is accurately predicted through the deployment of ED-BiGRU-LA, which enables the efficient processing and grasp long-term correlations within the sequential dataset. In this paper, the proposed method is evaluated by using two datasets and analyzed in comparison with other algorithms. The results show that the prediction framework demonstrates excellent performance with outstanding accuracy, robustness and generalization.

articleTitle: Mobility STAR-RIS-Assisted Indoor NOMA Networks Maximizing Secrecy Energy Efficiency Study
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Compared to traditional RIS, STAR-RIS has a wider coverage and is more valuable in complex environments. Exploiting the potential of STAR-RIS in MIMO-assisted NOMA systems, this paper proposes a mobile passive STAR-RIS-assisted indoor secure communication system designed to maximize the security energy efficiency (SEE) of the system. Since the resulting problem is non-convex, we perform the optimization of the two sub-problems by alternating iterations. Specifically, the Gd-Dinkelbach algorithm is designed to solve the beamforming optimization subproblem under fixed phase shift, and the original problem is correspondingly transformed into the secrecy maximization problem after its solution is obtained. On this basis, the PSO algorithm is innovatively applied to optimize the phase shift and amplitude in STAR-RIS. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in the proposed environment, and clearly show the influence of various parameter factors on the final result.

articleTitle: User Experience and Fuzzy Evaluation for Intelligent Cockpit
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: An intelligent cockpit user experience evaluation model is introduced, utilizing a three-level indicator system based on the fuzzy analytic hierarchy process. The first-level indicators encompass hardware, software functionality, perceptual experience, and emotional experience. Hardware and software, being fundamental cockpit's features, are pivotal to the overall user experience. Based on this, multimodal perceptual experience enhances user awareness and emotional experience reflects the user's psychological acceptance of the entire interaction process and outcomes, representing the culmination of the user's experience within the intelligent cockpits. Experimental results show that, when faced with numerous evaluation indicators, the proposed method outperforms traditional approaches, offering greater efficiency and reducing human subjectivity and uncertainty, thereby facilitating user experience evaluation. The studies presented can guide the user experience design for automobile intelligent cockpits.

articleTitle: Lunar Surface Target Detection Based on Improved YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In lunar exploration and research, the accurate identification and localization of lunar surface features is of great scientific significance and application value. However, target detection in lunar surface images faces a series of difficulties. Firstly, the lunar surface rock and soil is relatively monotonous and lacks texture information. Secondly,amount of image data on the lunar surface is less compared to most of the image data and there are overlapping areas between the images. Therefore, manually labeling lunar surface features is susceptible to significant errors. Thirdly, the size of the target in the lunar surface images is small and the resolution of the panorama spliced images of the lunar surface is high, leading to small target detection on high-resolution images a major technical difficulty. Aiming at the difficulty of data annotation of lunar surface images, this paper proposes a data annotation method based on panoramic spliced images. Then an improved YOLOv8 target detection algorithm is proposed by introducing an EMA(Expectation-Maximization-Attention) attention mechanisms, an adaptive feature fusion module and a sliding window based slice detection strategy, which solves the difficulty of detecting small targets on high-resolution images and avoids the problems of false detection and missed detection.

articleTitle: Research on Assisted Driving Method for Cotton Pickers Based on RTK-GPS
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In the large-area cotton picking operation, the traditional manual operation mode faces the problems of high labor intensity, slow operation speed and low efficiency. In order to solve these problems, this study proposes an automatic alignment method of cotton picker based on RTK-GPS trajectory navigation technology. This method first completes the alignment of the first row by manual operation, and then uses the segmented median filtering technology to record the trajectory data of RTK-GPS, and determines the slope of the reference navigation line by linear fitting these data. In the subsequent picking process, the cotton picker can automatically align with the target line from any starting point. This process depends on the initial coordinates and the determined reference line slope to calculate the parallel navigation baseline. Automatic alignment is realized by a speed adaptive pure tracking path algorithm. The field test results show that this method can realize the automatic line alignment from any starting position, and the system performance is superior to the traditional manual alignment mode in many aspects, which meets the requirements of the alignment accuracy of the cotton picker.

articleTitle: Daily Activity Recognition with Gait Segmentation and Hybrid Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Recent research has revealed that plantar pressure can reflect human characteristics, showing great potential in the field of biometrics. This study aims to explore the feasibility and methodology of using plantar pressure for daily activity recognition. We collected more than 10,000 pressure data points from 10 volunteers using insoles equipped with 8 pressure sensors to construct a dataset. Building upon a single Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), we introduced a hybrid network model combining Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Attention mechanisms, and evaluated its performance. Additionally, we analyzed the relationship between gait segmentation, the length of multiple gait cycles, and recognition accuracy. The experimental results showed that without segmentation based on gait cycles, the accuracy of classification using a single CNN was 95.0%, while the accuracy using the hybrid neural network was 97.0%. After segmenting based on gait cycles, the accuracy of classification using a single CNN reached 97.4%, and the hybrid neural network achieved an accuracy of 99.6%. These results indicate that classifying segmented gait data using a hybrid neural network can achieve superior outcomes, demonstrating significant practical value.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation and Feature Localization for Near-Infrared Cameras Calibration
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The Near-Infrared Camera(NIRC) is insensitive to the visible light spectrum. The lack of corresponding calibration device and extraction method of the feature points limit its application. Based on this, We design a near-infrared calibration device by attaching LEDs to the printed circuit board through Surface Mounted Technology(SMT). However, near-infrared LEDs generate scattering halos when powered on, so we improved this adverse effect by applying a Gaussian Convolution Kernel. Then, we detected subpixel edges of the feature points based on Zernike Moment. Finally, we perform ellipse fitting on subpixel edges to obtain more accurate center coordinates of the feature points.

articleTitle: Edge-Guided Network for Salient Object Detection in Substation Equipment Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the rapid development of computer vision, defect detection leveraging this technology has become an increasingly prominent trend. However, due to the interference from complex substation environments, traditional networks exhibit certain limitations in edge detection and defect information extraction. To address these challenges, this paper proposes the Edge-Guided Attention Network (EGANet), which consists of the Feature Extraction Module (FEM), the Edge Detection Module (EDM), and the Edge-Guided Attention Module (EGM). The FEM employs dilated convolutions with varying receptive fields to capture multi-scale contextual information. The EDM utilizes the Sobel operator, guided by high-level semantic features, to extract edge information from defect features. Meanwhile, the EGM integrates edge features and multi-scale features to further enhance critical edge information while suppressing irrelevant small structures. Experimental results demonstrate that EGANet performs exceptionally well in substation equipment defect detection tasks, surpassing state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy, generalization capability, and robustness.

articleTitle: Research on Big Data Financial Fraud Detection System Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: To solve the problem of fraud detection in financial transaction data, this paper proposes an innovative detection scheme that integrates machine learning and big data analysis technology. We combine the subtleties of time series analysis with the power of modern data analysis to design a model that is both efficient and accurate in identifying financial fraud. First, advanced data acquisition technology is used to capture high-frequency financial transaction data in real time to ensure the freshness and integrity of data. Then, the ARIMA (autoregressive integral moving average) model is used to analyze these time series data in depth to reveal the hidden information behind the trading patterns and trends. On this basis, the LightGBM (Lightweight Gradient Elevator) algorithm is introduced, which is a machine learning tool that performs well when dealing with high-dimensional, sparse data, especially for complex data structures in the financial sector. By integrating the time series features mined by ARIMA with multi-dimensional information such as credit history and geographical location of both parties, as the input of LightGBM model, we construct a multi-modal fraud detection framework. Empirical research shows that compared with using ARIMA model alone or traditional machine learning methods, our hybrid model has achieved a significant breakthrough in the accuracy and response speed of fraud detection, which can not only perceptively capture abnormal transaction activities, but also proactively warn potential financial risk points.

articleTitle: Engineering Vehicle Object Segmentation Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8x-seg
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: To address the challenges of low segmentation accuracy caused by complex backgrounds and relatively small objects in engineering vehicle images, this paper proposes a YOLO-based network, HFF-YOLO, that leverages high-frequency information fusion in the frequency domain. Building on the YOLOv8-seg segmentation network, the High-Frequency Information Extraction module (HFIE) is introduced, transforming images from the spatial domain to the frequency domain. By applying a high-pass filter, the HFIE integrates high-frequency information to achieve precise object edge segmentation in complex backgrounds. Subsequently, a Asymptotic Feature Pyramid Network is employed to construct a shallow segmentation head, and an Adaptive Spatial Feature Fusion module is introduced to address the issue of information loss caused by direct interactions between non-adjacent layers, thereby enabling more effective extraction and fusion of features across different levels. Finally, an engineering vehicle dataset, ENV3K, was constructed by collecting images under power transmission lines, and comparative experiments were conducted. Experimental results demonstrate that HFF-YOLO exhibits significant improvement in small object segmentation compared to YOLOv8x-seg, particularly achieving a 4.7% increase in mAP50 for crane boom segmentation. Additionally, the parameter count of HFF-YOLO is two-thirds that of the original YOLOv8x-seg model.

articleTitle: An Improved Adversarial Convolutional Transformer Model for Time Series Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Time series forecasting, as an important research topic in time series analysis, plays a crucial role in many fields. Traditional Transformer model often suffers from low feature dimension extraction and poor generalization ability when performing time series forecasting tasks. To address these issues, this paper proposes an Improved Adversarial Convolutional Transformer (IACT) model for time series forecasting. First, multi-dimensional features are extracted using the multi-head attention mechanism, and then more features are captured by multi-dimensional convolutional subspace in different dimensions to improve the representation capabilities of features. Meanwhile, an adversarial training strategy is used to make the model adapt to a larger range of data variations, which makes the model have a stronger generalization ability. Finally, experiment results conducted on two real time series datasets show that the model can obtain excellent prediction effects and generalization performance. In addition, the proposed model outperforms benchmark models such as Transformer, Pyraformer, and Informer in terms of prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: FvMamba: Super-Resolution Reconstruction Technology of Finger Vein Based on UNet-Like Mamba
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: To address the issue of elevated false detection rates in finger vein recognition, which arise from blurred images due to external environmental factors and hardware limitations during image acquisition, we propose a U-Net-based super-pixel image reconstruction method for finger veins utilizing Mamba blocks. This approach integrates Mamba blocks into the decoder to effectively capture long-range dependencies within the images, enhances the model's receptive fields, and better preserves the linear texture features characteristic of finger vein images. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method significantly improves the quality of finger vein images. When compared with SRCNN, EDSR, and FSRCNN methods on the FV-USM dataset, our approach exhibits superior performance in feature extraction as well as higher quality reconstructed images, achieving improved PSNR and SSIM metrics relative to other techniques.

articleTitle: The Method of Object Saliency Detection in Remote Sensing Images Based on Gestalt Theory and Visual Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: There are some shortcomings in existing salient object detection methods of remote sensing images. For example, the extracting features are insufficient and they are always seriously interfered by complex background information. To solve these problems, a visual attention model based on Gestalt theory is proposed. First, a pyramid anisotropic scale space model is built, followed by the extraction of multi-scale, multi-directional low-and high-frequency visual features to construct multi-space saliency maps. Then each spatial saliency map can be adaptively fused based on the similarity principle of Gestalt theory. Comparison and analysis are implemented among our proposed method and some existing methods on the public natural image dateset ECSSD and remote sensing image dateset ORSSD. The experimental results show that the proposed method has higher detection accuracy than existing saliency detection methods, especially in the detection of remote sensing images. It is greatly demonstrated that the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Journalists' Technological Trust and Willingness to Use Generative AI: A Perspective Based on Risk Perception Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This study explores the impact of perceived risk and trust on the willingness of journalists to use generative AI (GenAl) technology. As AI evolves, its applications in journalism, such as automated news writing and personalized content recommendations, have grown significantly. However, the adoption of GenAl by journalists is influenced by various factors, with perceived risk and trust being paramount. Perceived risk encompasses the uncertainties and potential negative outcomes associated with using the technology, while trust pertains to the confidence in the technology's reliability, security, and effectiveness. This research aims to fill the gap in empirical studies on these factors by constructing a theoretical model based on risk perception and trust theories. The study employs a detailed survey, validated through confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), to measure journalists' perceived risks, trust, and their willingness to use GenAl. Findings from this research are expected to offer valuable insights for the journalism industry, providing strategies to mitigate perceived risks and enhance trust, thereby promoting broader adoption of GenAl. Additionally, the results will contribute to the theoretical understanding of technology adoption in journalism and other professional domains.

articleTitle: Change Detection Method of High Resolution Remote Sensing Image Based on UNet Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: To address the issues of inadequate feature extraction, complicated models, and a large number of network parameters, this paper proposes a change detection method for high-resolution remote sensing images based on UNet network. Firstly, Resnet50 network is selected in the encoder part to obtain deeper features, avoid gradient disappearance and reduce training time. The scSE attention module structure is introduced in the skip connection. This module enhances the network's ability to prioritize the important channels and mine the local information better. Then, in order to improve the segmentation accuracy and obtain the context information better, atrous spatial pyramid pool is carried out in the deepest feature layer of the encoder to enrich the representation of information and obtain the multi-scale information of the target. Finally, the combination of Focal loss function and BCE loss weight was presented with improving model learning strategy. On the LEVIR-CD and CDD datasets, it is shown that proposed method has improved precision rate, recall rate and F1, and the number of model parameters is 5.37M, which is superior to other commonly used change detection networks.

articleTitle: A Novel Digital and Intelligent Automatic Kebab Machine Based on Grilling Recommendation Model
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In a fast-paced contemporary life, people pay more attention to the rapidity of food. Kebab as a kind of food is loved by people, at present many kebab store dining efficiency is low, kebabs are in short supply, while the existing kebab equipment in the level of intelligence is still deficient, unable to meet the needs of consumers and investors. In order to solve the above problems, grilling automation can be realized with the help of intelligent grilling methods. In this paper, we design a new digital and intelligent kebab grilling machine based on the grilling recommendation model, which combines hardware design and software development to improve efficiency through intelligent grilling. We designed a kebab machine with a layered architecture, which not only has the function of grilling but also can monitor the grilling process in real-time. The software platform receives the kebab matching queue through an external interface and generates matching information through the bake recommendation model, which is displayed on the interface of the software platform. The kebab machine interacts with the software platform in real-time and uploads the kebab process data to the software platform for statistics and storage. Based on these data, data visualization tools are used to analyze the changes in the ripeness of different types of kebabs and to study the relationship between grilling time, grilling temperature, and kebab ripeness.

articleTitle: MultiEdge-ResDeepLab: A Deep Learning Architecture for Multi-Modal Medical Image Segmentation with Enhanced Edge Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In the field of automatic image segmentation, especially for multi-modal medical images, precise segmentation of key structures is essential for accurate disease diagnosis and treatment. This study presents a novel deep learning architecture-MultiEdge-ResDeepLab-that combines edge enhancement with multi-modal segmentation techniques to boost performance. By incorporating edge enhancement using the Sobel operator and multi-scale feature fusion, the model improves its ability to capture finer details. Additionally, the use of dilated convolutions and ASPP modules expands the receptive field, allowing the model to capture richer contextual information and better hanle images at various scales. Experiments on the brats20 multi-modal medical image dataset demonstrate that MultiEdge-ResDeepLab outperforms existing methods in segmenting whole tumor (WT), tumor core (TC), and enhancing tumor (ET) areas. After 300 training rounds, the model achieved a Dice coefficient reached 0.959, showing a significant improvement in segmentation accuracy. The results highlight that combining edge information with multi-scale features can improve segmentation performance in complex medical applications. MultiEdge-ResDeepLab not only improves segmentation precision but also provides new directions for image processing research.

articleTitle: Research on Three-Dimensional Failure Envelope Surface of Composite Materials Based on Data-driven
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Data-driven methods based on machine learning have been successfully used in composite material design, structural analysis, data processing, material performance characterization, prediction and testing, and other fields. There is no theory in the field of composite material applications that can provide high-precision failure analysis and prediction results in all situations. This paper designed a biaxial compression-compression test of composite materials to obtain multi-variable data such as DIC digital speckle data, testing machine load-displacement data, and strain data. For the multidimensional data generated by the biaxial test, a fusion algorithm based on machine learning was used to construct a three-dimensional failure envelope of the composite material. The results show that the data mining methods can identify correlations in failure data and express them in the form of three-dimensional stress function equations. Data-driven methods based on physical information can further improve the accuracy of composite material failure behavior prediction and provide a technical basis for failure analysis and strength prediction of composite material structures.

articleTitle: Enhancing Brain Tumor Diagnosis with MedMamba: A Novel Application in Neural Imaging Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Brain tumors pose a great threat to human health and need to be diagnosed at an early stage. MRI plays an important role in assisting diagnosis due to its clear soft tissue visualization. Currently, the application of deep learning techniques in medical imaging shows the possibility of outperforming humans in terms of diagnostic accuracy and speed. This study explores the application of transfer learning and MedMamba models for brain tumor diagnosis, with a particular focus on their role in performing MRI brain tumor image classification. The MedMamba model is introduced and evaluated, which is a new adaptation of the Mamba framework optimized for the medical imaging field. This study not only compares the performance of MedMamba models with traditional deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Network and Vision Transformer, but also highlights the effectiveness of transfer learning in improving these models for specialized tasks in medical diagnosis. The main purpose is to describe the performance optimization capabilities provided by transfer learning and to demonstrate the inherent advantages of the MedMamba model. The model combines an innovative design with a streamlined architecture for efficient image processing. The positive role of transfer learning in the task of brain tumor image classification and the potential of MedMamba to set a new benchmark in this area are highlighted through comprehensive testing and evaluation of results on a brain MRI image dataset.

articleTitle: Optimizing LSTM, Bi-LSTM, and GRU Models with SSA for Daily Electricity Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Precise forecasting of electricity demand is vital for enhancing energy efficiency and ensuring grid stability. This research extends previous work by integrating Singular Spectrum Analysis (SSA) with enhanced deep learning architectures-specifically, dual-layered Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Longitudinal and Bidirectional LSTM networks have been enhanced through Dropout regularization and Multi-Head Attention mechanisms. The dataset utilized, sourced from the 2016 Electrical Engineering Cup, spans from January 2, 2012, to January 10, 2015, incorporating preprocessing like the exclusion of outliers and filling in missing values. The models show significant improvements in predictive accuracy: the SSA-enhanced BiLSTM model notably achieved an RMSE of 0.1050 and an R2 of 0.7085, a considerable improvement over the original BiLSTM model (RMSE 0.1395, R2 0.4898). Similarly, SSA-enhanced GRU and LSTM models demonstrated substantial performance gains over their original counterparts. modifications enhance the models' capability to effectively discern complex time series patterns, resulting in forecasts that are both more precise and dependable. The advancements underscore the potential of sophisticated model architectures in optimizing electricity demand management and advancing sustainable energy practices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Entity Aware-Interaction Network
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper addresses a significant challenge in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL): the paradoxical underperformance of theoretically superior algorithms like QTRAN compared to simpler ones such as QMIX and VDN in practical applications. We identify the root cause as inefficient network representations in QTRAN implementations. To resolve this, we propose a novel, high-efficiency network structure incorporating relational graph network and attention graph network modules. This structure significantly enhances QTRAN's sample efficiency and overall performance. By conceptualizing multi-agent systems as graph structures, our approach enables more effective representation of agent interactions and relationships. Experimental results demonstrate that our enhanced QTRAN outperforms state-of-the-art algorithms like QMIX and VDN in benchmark environments. This work contributes to bridging the gap between theoretical advancements and practical performance in MARL, particularly in fully cooperative tasks.

articleTitle: PHN: PointHeatNet for Point Clouds Classification and Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In recent years, point cloud learning has gained significant attention in fields such as computer vision, autono-mous driving, and robotics. The unordered and sparse nature of point cloud data makes traditional 2D image processing methods difficult to apply directly. The emergence of the PointNet model enabled end-to-end learning of point cloud data by proposing a new method to process unordered point clouds directly. Subse-quently, PointNet++ improved local feature learning through a hierarchical abstraction approach, but it still faces challenges such as high computational complexity and limited generalization capability. To further enhance the performance of point cloud feature extraction, this paper proposes the PointHeat network, inspired by the vHeat model based on the heat conduction equation used in 2D image processing. PointHeat leverages the Heat Conduction Operator (HCO) to process point cloud features in the frequency domain, achieving superior local and global feature extraction capabilities. Experimental results show that PointHeat improves accuracy by 1.7% in classification tasks and 1.2% in segmentation tasks, effectively enhancing the analytical performance of point cloud data.

articleTitle: Conceptual Design of Virtual Avatars Based on Intelligent Human-Machine Interface in Autonomous Driving
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This study explores the conceptual design of virtual avatars in autonomous driving and their trigger mechanisms in the context of the Intelligent Human-Machine Interface (HMI). Through the intelligent system's perception of the situation, virtual avatars can be dynamically triggered based on vehicle status, environmental information, and driver behavior, enabling precise information delivery and real-time feedback. The research indicates that users have high expectations for virtual avatars in terms of safety notifications, emotional expression, and personalized design. This study provides a reference for the design of virtual avatars in future autonomous driving systems and proposes prospects for further adaptive optimization.

articleTitle: A Visual Monitoring Method for Monochromators Based on Video Super-Resolution and Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: To achieve real-time and precise monitoring of the main moving component of the monochromator. We have developed a visual monitoring system for monochromator based on machine vision technology for SSRF. To enhance the accuracy and stability of visual detection, this paper proposes a visual monitoring method that integrates video super-resolution (VSR) and kalman filter (KF) with YOLOv5 object detection. First, VSR is applied to enhance the quality of images captured by the camera. Then, scale numbers on a ruler are detected, and KF is employed for stable tracking of the scale numbers' detection boxes. Finally, the position of the monitored subjects is calculated based on tracking results of the scale numbers on the ruler. Experimental results demonstrate that by implementing VSR, the detection rate of scale numbers improved by an average of 12%, and in combination with the tracking algorithm based on KF, the proposed method achieves enhanced stability in the positioning of the moving component in the monochromator.

articleTitle: Energy Consumption Optimization Scheme for UAV- Assisted NOMA-MEC Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The integration of Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) technology with Mobile Edge Computing (MEC), supported by UAVs, has emerged as a cutting-edge solution for enhancing uplink task offloading transmission performance. In this paper, we propose an optimized Successive Interference Cancellation (SIC) order that takes into account both channel gain and the urgency of offloading tasks, aiming to further minimize system energy consumption while satisfying task delay constraints. Given that this problem is a complex non-convex optimization challenge, we employ a Successive Convex Approximation (SCA) algorithm to alternately optimize two subproblems, progressively approaching the optimal solution. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme can significantly reduce system energy consumption.

articleTitle: Real-Time EMG Control for Assistive Devices: Optimizing Sensor Placement for Foot Drop Rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Foot drop, a condition that impairs foot mobility due to weakened dorsiflexor muscles, increases the risk of falls and unstable gait. This study investigates the use of electromyography (EMG) signals from functional muscles to control assistive devices for individuals with foot drop, focusing on optimal sensor placement for accurate signal acquisition. Using Arduino-based hardware and MATLAB algorithms, EMG signals were recorded from targeted muscles during controlled ankle movements, with Butterworth filtering and smoothing applied to enhance signal clarity. A 3D virtual actuation model demonstrated real-time control of object movements based on EMG data, achieving a strong correlation (R = 0.968) between EMG amplitude and actuator precision. These results suggest that accurate EMG-based control is feasible for developing effective assistive devices, improving mobility in individuals with foot drop.

articleTitle: CKDNet: A Cascaded Knowledge Distillation Framework for Lightweight Stereo Matching
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient cascaded knowledge distillation framework which is tailored for the refinement of lightweight stereo matching network. Lightweight network is the feasible means to achieve real-time depth estimation on embedded devices, but often suffered from reduced accuracy. Despite previous attempts to enhance performance through the introduction of new modules, the resulting improvements are modest. To address this challenge, our framework integrates knowledge distillation with three models to cascaded optimize the performance of lightweight architectures. Our contributions include three folds: First, we demonstrate the effectiveness of knowledge distillation for stereo matching and its transferability across different scale models. Second, we conduct a comprehensive comparison of distillation methods and propose the cascade distillation framework to improve the accuracy of lightweight model. Third, we proposed an adjustable compression module to enable flexible changes of model size by demands. Through extensive experimentation and evaluation, we validate the efficacy of our approach. Our lightweight model has archived 0.87px on Sceneflow(EPE), and 2.26% on KITTI2015(D1). And only 12 ms for a single-time inference.

articleTitle: MSCANet: A Multi-Branch Space Cross Attention Network for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In recent years, with the wide application of U-Net network architecture combined with channel or spatial attention mechanism in the field of medical image segmentation, the segmentation accuracy has been greatly improved. Among them, the channel or spatial attention mechanism can be more effective in extracting feature representations. However, for cross-channel network relations, if only channel dimension reduction operation is carried out, there is a high probability that some features of depth vision will be lost. Therefore, in this paper, we propose MSCANet, a multi-branch cross-spatial U-shaped attention network that preserves features on each channel while maintaining low computation. We have conducted extensive experiments on CVC-ClinicDB, 2018 Data Science Bowl and ISI-2018 datasets to verify the effectiveness and robustness of MSCANet in medical image segmentation tasks.

articleTitle: Target Tracking Algorithm Based on Variational Bayes
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: To address the problem of low tracking accuracy caused by unknown excitation and measurement noise in radar systems, a tracking algorithm based on variational Bayes is proposed. This algorithm leverages variational Bayes theory to treat the unknown excitation and measurement noise as hidden variables, enabling the computation of the likelihood probability of the target motion state. By decoupling these hidden variables under the expected maximum criterion and field theory, an approximate estimation of the hidden variables is obtained. These estimates are then combined with the unscented Kalman filter to achieve target state estimation. Through iterative updates of the target state, excitation, and measurement noise parameters, high-precision target tracking is achieved. Additionally, an evaluation method to terminate the iterative process is proposed. Simulation results demonstrate that the variational Bayes-based target tracking algorithm can effectively suppress tracking divergence issues caused by unknown parameters, leading to stable tracking performance and significant improvements in target state estimation accuracy. The algorithm consistently achieves stable target tracking across various target motion models, measurement errors, noise errors, and iteration termination values. These results indicate that the proposed method holds promising potential for practical applications.

articleTitle: An Analysis Method of Angle and Transverse Velocity of Upstream and Downstream Flow of Bridge
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The analysis method and systematic research of upstream and downstream flow angle and lateral velocity of bridges are important contents in bridge design and hydrology research, which are very important to ensure navigation safety and hydrology safety. In this study, an innovative analysis method and system of upstream and downstream flow angle and lateral velocity of bridges are proposed, which provides a new research direction and practical tool for related fields. The core of the research lies in the detailed analysis and calculation of specific bridge design parameters and water flow conditions, so as to optimize the bridge design and ensure the harmonious coexistence of its structural safety and water environment. Through the above analysis and calculation, the angle between upstream and downstream of the bridge and the lateral velocity of the flow can be accurately calculated, which provides data support for the safe passage of ships behind the bridge.

articleTitle: A Sequence Recommendation Algorithm Based on GCN Network and Self-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Traditional recommendation systems primarily rely on collaborative filtering, which struggles to effectively capture the dynamic changes in user interests. Sequential recommendation addresses this limitation by considering both user interests and social relationships to enhance recommendation outcomes. This paper proposes a sequential recommendation algorithm based on Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) and self-attention mechanisms, termed GSRec. The algorithm utilizes GCN to extract features from both trusted and untrusted users, integrating these features with item features. Subsequently, self-attention mechanisms are employed to construct dynamic user interest features, taking into account the positive influence of trusted users and the negative influence of untrusted users. Finally, the dynamic user interest features are combined with the influence of social relationships to generate the user's future interest features.specifically, the input to the GCN includes a feature matrix and an adjacency matrix. For trusted users, the feature matrix consists of the trust levels of the top n trusted users, and the adjacency matrix represents the trust relationships among these users. For untrusted users, the feature matrix and adjacency matrix incorporate the trust and distrust levels of the top n untrusted users. Experimental results on the Epinions dataset validate the accuracy of GSRec, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving recommendation efficiency.

articleTitle: Generate Adversarial Network Traffic Based on TMUAP for Reversible Transmission of Data
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: With the constant change of network environment, traditional methods have been unable to meet the task of high-precision network traffic classification, and deep learning methods rely on efficient feature extraction and other advantages have been widely studied and applied. Network traffic classification based on deep learning can automatically extract traffic characteristics and has achieved excellent results in different classification tasks such as encrypted traffic and malicious traffic, but it also faces the threat of countering network traffic. Adversarial network traffic is generated by adding adversarial perturbation to normal network traffic, which can attack the deep learning classifier and make its classification result predict wrong. Most of the adversarial network traffic generated by existing methods destroys the structural properties of network traffic and cannot achieve reversible data transmission of network traffic. An Adversarial network traffic generation algorithm Twice Modular Operation Universal Adversarial Perturbations (TM-UAP) is proposed in this paper, which realizes the reversible data transmission of adversarial network traffic. Thus, the effective attack on the network traffic classifier and the data availability of both the sender and receiver of network traffic are realized. Finally, this paper selects the commonly used standard network traffic data sets ISCX20 16 and USTC- TFC2016 to conduct simulation experiments on LeNet5, CNN and other classification models. The results show that the proposed method can not only effectively attack network traffic classifiers, but also achieve reversible data transmission of network traffic. It provides a new method for the practical application research of countering network traffic.

articleTitle: Supervised Data-Dependent Kernel Low-Rank Preserving Projection for Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Dimensionality reduction (DR) is a frequently used method to handle data with many dimensions. This article presents a novel approach to nonlinear dimensionality reduction, referred to as supervised data-dependent kernel low-rank preserving projection (SDKLRPP). Designed for image recognition tasks. The method enhances performance by utilizing a data-dependent kernel (DK). Unlike traditional nonlinear dimensionality reduction techniques, the SDKLRPP method described in this paper can fine-tune the coefficients within the DK and uncover The paper elucidates the low-rank reconstructive relationship inherent in the data. It also illustrates how the manifold structure within the feature space is mirrored in the label space, grounded in the principle of smoothness. This enables label information to direct the optimization of coefficients within the DK, thereby enhancing the capacity to discern among various classes. Upon attaining the optimal low-rank reconstructive relationship, a transformation matrix is computed to maintain this relationship, which is subsequently utilized to project the data into a reduced-dimensional space. The efficacy of the proposed SDKLRPP methodology is substantiated through experiments conducted on five extensively acknowledged databases.

articleTitle: Lightweight YOLOv8n with Cross-Scale Feature Fusion for Driver Fatigue Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Currently, most fatigue driving detection methods based on deep learning meet accuracy requirements. However, these models have a high number of parameters and require significant computation, resulting in low real-time speed. Hence, they cannot be applied to on-board equipment with limited memory and computing power. To address these issues, a lightweight network model was designed based on the YOLOv8n object detection network. The Down sampling module, which reduces the spatial resolution of feature maps to decrease the model's computational load and number of parameters, replaces the Convolution module in the traditional YOLOv8n model series. This module captures image features at a higher level using a specific Down sampling strategy. Additionally, a lightweight Cross-Scale Feature Fusion Module framework is further adopted in the neck to replace the original neck structure, reducing giga floating-point operations per second and enhancing the model's detection capabilities. The Focal Modulation technology was used to replace the original Spatial Pyramid Pooling Fast module, improving the model's recognition ability for these areas and solving the problem of reduced model accuracy caused by the lightweight design. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model effectively achieves lightweight effects. The improved model shows a 1.1 % increase in accuracy, a 42.2 % decrease in the number of parameters, a 27.1 % decrease in computation, and a 40.6% reduction in model size. Moreover, the model accurately extracts the driver's eyes and mouth opening characteristics. The eye closure index percentage is used to objectively and accurately assess a driver's fatigue, providing an early warning to the driver.

articleTitle: TASFNet: Robust Point Cloud Correspondence via Topological and Semantic Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In the field of point cloud registration, the extraction of correspondences of low-overlap point clouds is still a difficult challenge, and its results have a decisive influence on the quality of the registration. Although current methods have made significant progress in solving this problem, the abnormal matching problem is still a major bottleneck, limiting the accuracy and reliability of registration. Based on this, we innovatively proposed TASF (Topological and Semantic Framework), which captures the topological structure and semantic features of point clouds at the same time, thereby revealing the deep information hidden in the point cloud, and can achieve high-quality point correspondence even under low overlap conditions. The superiority of TASF has been fully verified on two point cloud registration datasets, 3DMatch and 3DLoMatch. Especially in the test of low-overlap datasets such as 3DLoMatch, our method significantly improved the matching ratio of points in the point cloud, up to 8.8 percentage points higher than the existing methods. This result verifies the feasibility of our method.

articleTitle: SAPAD- AHP- QFD-Based Emotional Cockpit Design Study for Novice Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In this study, the SAPAD-AHP-QFD fusion research method is used to obtain information about novice drivers' needs for smart cockpits, and transform them into design features to propose practical solutions to improve the driving experience and emotional satisfaction of novice drivers. Firstly, the daily behavior information of novice drivers is obtained through observation and interview, and the mapping analysis of “behavior-product-meaning” is completed according to SAPAD theory, and user needs are extracted through cluster analysis; secondly, the weight analysis of user needs is carried out by using the AHP method, and the weight value of each need is obtained; finally, the quality of the intelligent emotional cockpit is constructed according to the QFD theory, and the design features are transformed into design features to propose practical solutions to improve the driving experience and emotional satisfaction of novice drivers. Finally, the QFD theory is used to construct the quality house of the intelligent emotional cockpit, and the user requirements are transformed into specific design features to guide the design practice. The results of the study show that novice drivers often experience negative emotions such as nervousness and fear when driving, and in order to alleviate this emotion, it is necessary to introduce affective computing technology as the support of interaction design in the smart cockpit scenario. At the same time, the study also provides a theoretical and practical system for constructing a research path for product and interaction design based on affective computing technology.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Age Differences on Interface Design Features
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This research explores the design of smart washing machine interfaces, aiming to improve universality and user experience. The study involved 32 participants from different age groups who tested a prototype interface developed using Axure and Figma software. Eye tracking technology and subjective preference questionnaires were used to analyze user differences and preferences. Results showed that both age groups performed better with a list-based interface layout. Younger users preferred single-color interfaces and flat icons, while older users preferred interfaces with adjacent colors, realistic icons, and sound feedback. Designers and engineers should consider these findings to improve product universality and optimize user experience.

articleTitle: Equipment Health Status Assessment Based on Belief Rule Base and Hidden Markov Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In order to solve the problems of high dimension and large scale of multi-sensor monitoring data and low-accuracy prediction in the remaining useful life (RUL) of nonlinear degradation equipment, a degradation index construction method based on Hidden Markov model (HMM) is proposed, and combined with the belief rule base (BRB) reasoning method to evaluate the health status and realize the RUL prediction. Firstly, the Gaussian HMM is established by taking a variety of performance parameters in the equipment life cycle as the observation vector, and then the equipment performance degradation process is simulated. Secondly, the degradation index is used as the label to train the BRB model, and then the automatic evaluation of equipment health state can be realized. Finally, the RUL is calculated by the BRB-HMM hybrid model. To validate the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed approach, a case study is carredout on the NASA's commercial modular aero-propulsion system simulation datasets.

articleTitle: ALPSolver: A Solver for Assumable Logic Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Assumable Logic Programming (ALP), an extension of Answer Set Programming (ASP), has been theoretically demonstrated to possess significant advantages in addressing problems involving incomplete information. Therefore, the development of ALP solvers is urgently needed to facilitate further research and applications. This paper proposes a solving algorithm named Answer Set Based View Search (ASBVS) and its optimization to compute the results of ALP programs. Based on this, the ALPSolver has been implemented and integrated into an online platform for public use. This paper experimentally validates the correctness of the solving algorithm and confirms the advantages of ALP in handling default information, indirect exception and abductive reasoning. Additionally, the experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the optimization algorithm, with a notable increase in efficiency as the problem scale increases.

articleTitle: A Healthcare Data Sharing Scheme Based on Homomorphic Encryption and Federated Metric Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Medical data is highly sensitive, often leading to “data silos” in sharing processes. To address this issue, this paper combines blockchain and federated metric learning technologies, and innovatively integrates them with homomorphic encryption technology to propose a privacy protection system suitable for application in medical data sharing scenarios. The system employs federated learning to train a global model across distributed client nodes without sharing raw data. Metric learning classifies clients as benign or malicious based on data similarity, only aggregating models from benign clients to improve efficiency and mitigate data distribution issues. Additionally, differential privacy and homomorphic encryption are used to further protect data privacy by preventing the original data from being reverse deduced and model parameter leakage during aggregation. Experimental results show that the system can achieve a prediction accuracy of 89.102564% under different data distributions, and its performance on medical datasets has been significantly improved compared to traditional federated learning.

articleTitle: Research on Interactive Digital Garden Design Based on Emotional Design
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: In today's rapidly developing digital era, people are increasingly seeking to integrate natural elements into their living and working environments for emotional comfort and aesthetic enhancement. In response to the monolithic nature of traditional plant interactions, this study introduces “PhotonFloral”, an interactive digital garden designed based on emotional design principles. The system integrates Unity and Arduino technologies to provide a highly realistic virtual environment and a rich interactive experience, aiming to overcome the limitations of traditional potted plants. Based on this, we conducted a series of tests and interviews, and the results show that PhotonFloral has great potential in providing emotional companionship and landscaping. In addition, this paper shares in detail its research, design, and development process, inspiring other designs designed to improve indoor environments and enrich emotional life.

articleTitle: DFL-PVNet: A Lightweight Photovoltaic Hotspot Detection Network Based on Dynamic Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Photovoltaic (PV) panels are vital for renewable energy, but are prone to hotspot faults during operation, which can reduce dependability and cause safety risks. Conventional hotspot detection techniques are often hindered by high costs, intricate operations, and limited detection capabilities. In recent years, deep learning-based detection methods, particularly those leveraging infrared imaging, have demonstrated substantial promise. However, current models encounter challenges related to parameter complexity and limited flexibility in feature fusion, which impede their performance across varying operational conditions. Therefore, this study proposes the Dynamic Feature Fusion and Lightweight Photovoltaic Hotspot Detection Network (DFL-PVNet), which is based on an improved YOLOv8 structur. DFL-PVNet aims to reduce model parameters and computational complexity while optimizing feature fusion, thereby enhancing the accuracy and applicability of hotspot detection. Experimental results demonstrate that DFL-PVNet achieves superior performance in the hotspot detection of PV panels. Compared with baseline, the number of parameters and computation of DFL-PVNet decrease by 56.7% and 65.4%, and the recall, mAP@50 and mAP@50-95 increase by 14%, 11.6% and 5.4%, respectively, which are all better than the existing mainstream target detection methods.

articleTitle: Guidance Strategy for High-Speed Traversal of Fixed-Wing UAV Dense Formations
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Cluster guidance technology for fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has been a significant research focus in the UAV field. Cluster UAV guidance faces challenges such as mission coordination and path decision planning, while also needing to consider real-world scenarios and constraints. This paper addresses the visual guidance challenge of fixed-wing UAVs in dense formation scenarios, set against the backdrop of the Fast Crossing Race. Firstly, it analyzes the issues of visual blind spots and inter-vehicle occlusion during Fast Crossing Race in dense UAV formations. Secondly, we proposes a method based on the absolute pose of the gate frame to solve the problem of visual blind spots during close-range approaches. Additionally, a multi-source guidance information fusion strategy is designed to address the issue of inter-vehicle visual occlusion in dense formations. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed technology and strategy, a corresponding cluster fixed-wing UAV system was designed. The system, in the form of a dense formation of seven UAVs, achieved the highest score in the second “Unmanned Aerial Contest” Fast Crossing Race, demonstrating the feasibility and advancement of the proposed guidance strategy.

articleTitle: Active Learning in Industrial Defect Detection: A Dynamic Approach to Uncertainty and Representativeness
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The storage and annotation of industrial data is a costly and time-intensive work in developing a defects detector. To overcome this challenge, this study proposes an effective annotation workflow and an active learning strategy that integrates uncertainty and representativeness to construct a reliable defects detection model. The annotation workflow involves both the advisor and the labeling team for the inspection of industrial data that depends on specialized knowledge in a particular area. The active learning strategy combines the uncertainty-based and the representativeness-based sampling metrics flexibly to assess the informativeness of the unlabeled data. Besides, a training strategy for active learning models is used to address not only data uncertainty but also the generalization of feature distribution across all data. We benchmark the proposed method on Bottled Baijiu Defect Detection Dataset, utilizing RetinaNet as the baseline detector. Results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly reduces labeling costs and data storage requirements, which is crucial for industrial defect detection.

articleTitle: Behavior Recognition Algorithm for Electric Power Workers in Hazy Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of reduced recognition accuracy in the field of electric power worker behavior recognition due to the impact of hazy environments, which cause the images to become blurry and features to become less distinct. To tackle this problem, an algorithm based on Retinex algorithm and wavelet transform for haze removal, followed by the use of an improved YOLOv8 model for worker behavior recognition, is proposed to enhance the model's recognition capabilities in hazy environments. Initially, the input RGB image is converted to a YIQ image, and the Y component is extracted. Then, wavelet decomposition is applied to the Y component to separate the low-frequency component containing haze information and the high-frequency component containing image details. The Retinex algorithm is used for haze removal on the low-frequency component, while the high-frequency part is processed with a wavelet threshold function using a hard threshold function to suppress useless parts and enhance useful parts, preserving more features of the image. Finally, the processed low and high-frequency components are reconstructed through wavelet reconstruction to obtain the output image. This processed image is then used as input for the improved YOLOv8 model to recognize the specific behavior characteristics of electric power workers in the image. The specific improvements to the YOLOv8 model are as follows: the standard convolution in the original YOLOv8 bottleneck is replaced with deformable convolution, and the attention mechanism CBAM is added to construct a new bottleneck_den module, which replaces the bottleneck module in C2f of YOLOv8 and is renamed as C2f_DeN. Secondly, all standard convolutions in the backbone of YOLOv8 are replaced with deformable convolutions to enhance the model's ability to extract image features. Experiments show that the improved algorithm model has an mAP of 85.2%, which is an increase of 6.3 percentage points and 4.5 percentage points compared to two other models that have also been processed.

articleTitle: Research on Style Transfer Method from Human Facial Images to Peking Opera Facial Images
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: Face makeup transfer is designed to transfer the makeup features of one reference image to another face image to achieve the transformation of different makeup styles. Ordinary makeup has the characteristics of uniform color in a single area and simple color in the overall area, while opera facial makeup is mostly hand-painted images, rich in colors and textures. It is difficult for non-professional actors to draw. At present, there is no deep learning-based method to study makeup transfer between face and Peking Opera facial makeup images. In this paper, we proposes a facial makeup transfer method based on generative adversarial networks and affine transformation. We create a facial makeup dataset from Peking Opera facial makeup images, and obtains the corresponding mask dataset through a semantic segmentation feature extraction model for facial parsing. A local histogram matching strategy is used to calculate the pixel-level histogram loss, which can better preserve the color characteristics of the image. An auxiliary discriminant network is introduced to synthesize reference labels by performing affine transformation on Peking Opera facial makeup images and face images, which helps the generator network to better reduce the information loss caused by image transformation. Through the research in this paper, it is expected to contribute to the research and application of this field, and provide new possibilities for the protection and inheritance of traditional culture and art.

articleTitle: An Anonymous Identity Authentication Scheme Integrating Trust Determination for Cloud-Edge Collaborative Task Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
abstract: The traditional centralized cloud-based collaborative task scheduling model faces various challenges such as network latency, data confidentiality, and business flexibility. The integration of edge computing technology into cloud-edge collaborative task scheduling has become the current trend. With the transformation of scheduling models, the task scheduling environment further presents characteristics such as deep resource heterogeneity and complex task collaboration levels, leading to an increased risk of privacy leakage during the scheduling process. In response, an anonymous identity authentication scheme integrating trust determination for cloud-edge collaborative task scheduling is proposed. To address the potential malicious behaviors resulting from identity hijacking after secure device access, a comprehensive subjective and objective trust relationship model is introduced to discern malicious device actions and promptly revoke the anonymity of counterfeit devices, ensuring reliable scheduling execution. Additionally, to further achieve collaborative task scheduling objectives across resources, traffic, business, and security goals at the cloud-edge, the solution incorporates smart contract technology to regulate scheduling strategy execution and introduces blockchain for unified storage and management of critical scheduling records. Finally, through correctness analysis, security analysis, and efficiency analysis, the feasibility of the solution is validated.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Motor Imagery Decoding Combining Channel Attention and Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 5th International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Human-Computer Interaction (ICHCI)
